01:49:01,403 --> 01:49:03,702
people wouldn't think
that I'm a big game threat.

1789
01:49:03,843 --> 01:49:05,462
And if I wasn't
a big challenge threat,

1790
01:49:05,603 --> 01:49:07,022
they wouldn't think
I was a challenge threat.

1791
01:49:07,163 --> 01:49:09,582
And then, for me,
it was about making it to the end.

1792
01:49:09,723 --> 01:49:12,822
It was about, you know, changing
my life, changing my family's life,

1793
01:49:12,963 --> 01:49:15,742
and that was more important
than anything else.

1794
01:49:15,883 --> 01:49:18,102
Sharn, in perhaps
the most pivotal moment of the game,

1795
01:49:18,243 --> 01:49:23,422
you convinced AK, Shonee and Brooke
not to go to rocks.

1796
01:49:23,563 --> 01:49:25,742
- In that moment...
- Yep.

1797
01:49:25,883 --> 01:49:28,342
..what is it that you think you did
that changed their mind?

1798
01:49:28,443 --> 01:49:29,822
They looked so convinced.

1799
01:49:31,163 --> 01:49:35,182
Yeah, well, I think
I appealed to their common sense,

1800
01:49:35,283 --> 01:49:36,662
at the end of the day,

1801
01:49:36,803 --> 01:49:39,602
because it was a foolish thing
to go to rocks.

1802
01:49:39,723 --> 01:49:42,702
And, you know, it wasn't one of...
Like, it was for Jacqui.

1803
01:49:42,843 --> 01:49:46,062
I mean, they weren't
working with Jacqui for a long time.

1804
01:49:46,203 --> 01:49:48,622
I felt that
if I could persuade them,

1805
01:49:48,723 --> 01:49:51,462
they would see that logic and sense,

1806
01:49:51,563 --> 01:49:53,422
and they did.

1807
01:49:53,563 --> 01:49:56,342
If you had your time again, Shonee,
would you go to rocks?

1808
01:49:57,883 --> 01:50:00,582
I mean, I feel like Dave
playing the idol for Tarzan

1809
01:50:00,683 --> 01:50:02,182
really did reduce our odds.

1810
01:50:02,323 --> 01:50:05,462
But, I mean, I went out next anyway,
so maybe I should've taken a gamble.

1811
01:50:05,563 --> 01:50:07,102
Yeah, risk it for the biscuit.

1812
01:50:08,743 --> 01:50:11,242
Now, there is one
unforgettable Tribal

1813
01:50:11,323 --> 01:50:12,942
that we haven't touched on quite yet,

1814
01:50:13,043 --> 01:50:15,462
and that was Daisy's blindside,

1815
01:50:15,603 --> 01:50:20,782
orchestrated in secret
by the Golden God and the Godfather.

1816
01:50:21,943 --> 01:50:23,602
Being on the bottom is not fun.

1817
01:50:23,723 --> 01:50:26,822
Seven verse four has put me in
a pretty precarious position.

1818
01:50:28,603 --> 01:50:30,862
I've never really been in
a majority alliance before,

1819
01:50:30,963 --> 01:50:33,062
so this is a weird spot to be in.

1820
01:50:34,503 --> 01:50:37,142
I'm a big fan of unlikely duos.

1821
01:50:49,903 --> 01:50:53,542
We are the most unlikely alliance
in this game,

1822
01:50:53,643 --> 01:50:56,022
and they will never see us coming.

1823
01:50:59,843 --> 01:51:01,242
I think he is, man.

1824
01:51:02,523 --> 01:51:05,222
I'm gonna have to go to Dave
and put my entire game on the line.

1825
01:51:07,563 --> 01:51:10,822
You tell me who you're voting for,
I'll play the idol on them,

1826
01:51:10,963 --> 01:51:13,062
and then I'll vote out someone
out of your alliance.

1827
01:51:23,043 --> 01:51:24,962
If anyone has a hidden immunity idol

1828
01:51:25,083 --> 01:51:27,822
and you want to play it,
now would be the time to do so.

1829
01:51:29,223 --> 01:51:31,182
I might play it for...

1830
01:51:32,303 --> 01:51:34,542
..Jacqui.

1831
01:51:39,483 --> 01:51:41,982
Third person voted out of
Australian Survivor: All Stars...

1832
01:51:43,503 --> 01:51:44,682
..Daisy.

1833
01:51:52,883 --> 01:51:55,322
Now, unfortunately,
because of travel restrictions,

1834
01:51:55,443 --> 01:51:58,382
the Godfather, Mat Rogers,
couldn't be with us tonight,

1835
01:51:58,483 --> 01:52:00,542
but the Golden God is.

1836
01:52:00,643 --> 01:52:02,982
First of all, David, why...

1837
01:52:03,123 --> 01:52:06,322
Oh, great acting, by the way.
Great eye acting.

1838
01:52:06,443 --> 01:52:09,822
Why go to Mat Rogers with that plan?
Why not anybody else?

1839
01:52:09,963 --> 01:52:12,262
Oh, I think, like I was
talking about a bit earlier,

1840
01:52:12,403 --> 01:52:15,782
that I wanted to have
really unlikely alliances

1841
01:52:15,923 --> 01:52:18,182
and Mat probably being
the biggest villain

1842
01:52:18,283 --> 01:52:19,782
that Australian Survivor has seen

1843
01:52:19,963 --> 01:52:23,062
and me being the biggest hero,
it just seemed to make sense.

1844
01:52:23,203 --> 01:52:24,822
Um, and I really loved
Mat's game-play

1845
01:52:24,963 --> 01:52:28,862
the first time I watched him play
on his season.

1846
01:52:28,963 --> 01:52:30,462
And then I thought, "You know what?

1847
01:52:30,603 --> 01:52:33,322
"This is gonna be
some good stuff here."

1848
01:52:33,463 --> 01:52:37,042
Daisy, you were the unfortunate
collateral damage at that Tribal.

1849
01:52:37,123 --> 01:52:39,142
Did you have any idea it was coming?

1850
01:52:39,283 --> 01:52:42,982
Um, I did keep trying to
tell my sexy seven alliance

1851
01:52:43,083 --> 01:52:44,902
that we can't trust him

1852
01:52:45,043 --> 01:52:50,382
'cause I've played for a very
long time with Dave in our season

1853
01:52:50,523 --> 01:52:52,582
and I knew what
he was like as a player.

1854
01:52:52,723 --> 01:52:56,062
But everyone wanted to
keep holding on one more vote

1855
01:52:56,203 --> 01:53:00,782
and, uh, I was the collateral damage
and my heart was broken.

1856
01:53:02,483 --> 01:53:04,942
Well, Mat and David's partnership,

1857
01:53:05,043 --> 01:53:07,042
it would not have been as effective

1858
01:53:07,163 --> 01:53:09,302
without the help
of a hidden immunity idol.

1859
01:53:09,443 --> 01:53:12,542
But they weren't the only ones
who got to play with idols.

1860
01:53:13,763 --> 01:53:16,142
Shonee has the best position today.

1861
01:53:17,943 --> 01:53:19,342
In this game,

1862
01:53:19,443 --> 01:53:21,402
a hidden immunity idol is your life.

1863
01:53:21,523 --> 01:53:22,982
It can potentially save you
from going home...

1864
01:53:24,483 --> 01:53:26,742
..or save one of
your alliance members going home.

1865
01:53:30,223 --> 01:53:32,342
It's a really powerful tool.

1866
01:53:36,023 --> 01:53:40,102
Yes!

1867
01:53:40,203 --> 01:53:43,042
Oh, man, that feels good!

1868
01:53:43,163 --> 01:53:45,862
The Golden God
has risen again!

1869
01:53:46,003 --> 01:53:48,402
Urghhh!

1870
01:53:48,523 --> 01:53:51,142
If anyone has a hidden immunity idol
and you want to play it,

1871
01:53:51,243 --> 01:53:53,462
now would be the time to do so.

1872
01:53:55,483 --> 01:53:58,702
OK. Who are you playing this for?

1873
01:53:58,803 --> 01:54:01,142
I will play it for...David.

1874
01:54:01,243 --> 01:54:03,102
For David.

1875
01:54:03,243 --> 01:54:04,862
Thanks.
You're welcome.

1876
01:54:05,003 --> 01:54:08,702
Next minute,
I see, like, a little scroll.

1877
01:54:10,123 --> 01:54:12,782
I think I did it quite swiftly.

1878
01:54:12,883 --> 01:54:14,702
So I'm hoping no-one saw it.

1879
01:54:14,843 --> 01:54:18,422
"The idol you seek
is hidden underneath the well."

1880
01:54:23,723 --> 01:54:25,622
You serious?

1881
01:54:25,723 --> 01:54:26,723
Shh.

1882
01:54:33,963 --> 01:54:36,422
The look on everyone's face when you
find an idol right in front of them?

1883
01:54:38,963 --> 01:54:42,102
That's bullshit!

1884
01:54:42,203 --> 01:54:44,782
Priceless. Mwah.

1885
01:54:47,003 --> 01:54:49,942
Shonee, when did you actually realise

1886
01:54:50,083 --> 01:54:52,502
that the idol clue
was hidden under the bench?

1887
01:54:52,643 --> 01:54:54,402
Definitely not
when I was sitting on it.

1888
01:54:54,483 --> 01:54:56,662
It happened while I was watching TV

1889
01:54:56,803 --> 01:54:59,762
and I was like,
"No, dammit! If only!"

1890
01:54:59,883 --> 01:55:01,662
Were you yelling at your telly?
Yes.

1891
01:55:01,763 --> 01:55:03,182
But I also happy 'cause I'm like,

1892
01:55:03,323 --> 01:55:04,762
"Uh, meh, don't worry,
you get it tomorrow."

1893
01:55:07,763 --> 01:55:09,862
Of course we cannot talk about idols

1894
01:55:10,003 --> 01:55:14,942
without mentioning that David
basically stole one off Phoebe.

1895
01:55:15,083 --> 01:55:19,582
After the break, we'll see if
they've managed to patch things up.

1896
01:55:33,058 --> 01:55:35,629
The first thing that
goes through my mind is,

1897
01:55:35,635 --> 01:55:37,032
"Oh, my god there's a doughnut,"

1898
01:55:37,038 --> 01:55:39,550
followed by, "where the
hell is the idol clue."

1899
01:55:40,360 --> 01:55:42,782
I am going clockwise round the room,

1900
01:55:42,788 --> 01:55:46,764
tryin' to stuff my face with cake
and doughnuts at the same time,

1901
01:55:47,064 --> 01:55:51,257
and finally I get to, like,
the second last cake and...

1902
01:55:51,937 --> 01:55:54,532
..ha! The idol clue is there.

1903
01:55:54,538 --> 01:55:55,538
Cool.

1904
01:56:04,315 --> 01:56:05,863
If I was an idol...

1905
01:56:07,109 --> 01:56:09,032
..where would I be?!

1906
01:56:13,125 --> 01:56:14,172
Nothin'!

1907
01:56:19,919 --> 01:56:20,919
Nothing!

1908
01:56:24,592 --> 01:56:25,527
Yeah.

1909
01:56:25,533 --> 01:56:30,082
I actually cannot believe that
Phoebe is telling me about this clue.

1910
01:56:31,372 --> 01:56:34,532
- Yeah. It's in a termite mound.
- Oh, man!

1911
01:56:35,308 --> 01:56:39,266
Oh! Thank you. Thank you, Phoebe!

1912
01:56:39,272 --> 01:56:40,272
It's not down this one.

1913
01:56:40,278 --> 01:56:42,037
There's like three right
down the middle path there.

1914
01:56:42,240 --> 01:56:46,783
There's one termite mound that
needs to be searched <i>immediately</i>.

1915
01:56:52,724 --> 01:56:53,803
There it is!

1916
01:56:56,127 --> 01:56:57,422
Such a douche.

1917
01:56:57,428 --> 01:57:01,782
This is, like, straight up,
Iron Man's lasers right here.

1918
01:57:01,788 --> 01:57:04,411
People gonna be tryin' to blindside
me and I'm gonna be, like,

1919
01:57:04,412 --> 01:57:09,532
"Dzrum... dzrum... dzrum... dzrum!"

1920
01:57:11,383 --> 01:57:14,082
All Stars' Reunion Show,

1921
01:57:14,088 --> 01:57:16,287
we are on the topic of idols.

1922
01:57:16,375 --> 01:57:18,343
Phoebe, when you watched all that back,

1923
01:57:18,349 --> 01:57:21,782
when you saw how is actually
happened, how did it make you feel?

1924
01:57:22,835 --> 01:57:26,782
Oh, I think... it was hard to
relive, if I'm honest. Um...

1925
01:57:27,304 --> 01:57:30,282
I had... I had a bit of anxiety
leading up to that episode

1926
01:57:30,288 --> 01:57:33,351
because I knew, um, what the outcome
was, and I knew how it ended.

1927
01:57:33,357 --> 01:57:37,281
Obviously, David got that idol out
at the tribal that I left, um...

1928
01:57:37,294 --> 01:57:41,539
..so, yeah, it was hard to relive,
but at the end of the day, like,

1929
01:57:41,545 --> 01:57:43,561
you know, it still took
them a fire challenge

1930
01:57:43,567 --> 01:57:45,060
and a split vote to get me, um,

1931
01:57:45,066 --> 01:57:49,474
not withstanding David's flip, so,
you know, it was what it was.

1932
01:57:50,125 --> 01:57:52,768
So, how would you say things are
between the two of you at the moment?

1933
01:57:57,106 --> 01:57:58,717
You know, I'm good.

1934
01:57:58,731 --> 01:58:01,106
- Are you guys good?
- I... I mean, I'm good.

1935
01:58:01,112 --> 01:58:04,031
No, I think... I think we're
great, man. I, like...

1936
01:58:04,044 --> 01:58:05,532
I think part of the...

1937
01:58:05,538 --> 01:58:07,377
- I think he was asking her.
- Maybe I shouldn't answer this?

1938
01:58:07,663 --> 01:58:10,797
- Yeah, I was asking her.
- OK, I'll just stay out of it, alright?

1939
01:58:10,798 --> 01:58:12,711
How are things between the two of you?

1940
01:58:12,717 --> 01:58:15,988
Things are great. I mean... I...

1941
01:58:16,494 --> 01:58:19,089
..I'm a Survivor fan, and, um,

1942
01:58:19,095 --> 01:58:22,986
you know, look, it hurts to lose, of
course. Like, it hurts everything.

1943
01:58:22,992 --> 01:58:25,597
It hurts your pride, it hurts
your ego, it hurts your heart.

1944
01:58:25,603 --> 01:58:28,032
It really does hurt,
but, at the same time,

1945
01:58:28,038 --> 01:58:31,419
that's what the game is, and... David
is a phenomenal Survivor player,

1946
01:58:31,425 --> 01:58:33,369
and he... he won,

1947
01:58:33,375 --> 01:58:37,068
and I think he has played the
best game that we've seen, so...

1948
01:58:37,074 --> 01:58:38,893
..you can't really argue with that.

1949
01:58:40,092 --> 01:58:43,170
Flick, what would you have done
if you were in David's shoes?

1950
01:58:43,861 --> 01:58:46,060
I mean, I probably would
have done the same thing.

1951
01:58:46,066 --> 01:58:49,766
David is... such a
great player, he is...

1952
01:58:49,772 --> 01:58:51,623
You would not have done that to me!

1953
01:58:51,629 --> 01:58:54,962
Oh, OK, OK, maybe I wouldn't
have done it to Phoebe, nah.

1954
01:58:54,968 --> 01:58:57,153
I mean, I probably wouldn't
have done it to Phoebe...

1955
01:58:57,159 --> 01:59:00,532
- What about me?
- ..but I would have done it to Brooke.

1956
01:59:01,594 --> 01:59:05,752
No, but I definitely think that
what he did was right for his game.

1957
01:59:05,758 --> 01:59:08,783
Um, he made a bold move, and
it was a great move, and...

1958
01:59:08,789 --> 01:59:10,149
and look where it got him. He...

1959
01:59:10,155 --> 01:59:12,042
he got to the end and
he's won the game.

1960
01:59:12,608 --> 01:59:16,545
Well, this season wasn't
just intense game play...

1961
01:59:16,783 --> 01:59:19,901
..it was... it was highly emotional too.

1962
01:59:19,907 --> 01:59:22,878
Even for All Stars players
it's hard to prepare

1963
01:59:22,884 --> 01:59:24,640
for such a gruelling time

1964
01:59:24,646 --> 01:59:27,287
without your family and
your friends by your side.

1965
01:59:34,674 --> 01:59:35,816
Oh, Mo.

1966
01:59:36,023 --> 01:59:40,032
We are all out here fighting
like hell to win this game...

1967
01:59:45,212 --> 01:59:46,212
Oh!

1968
01:59:46,218 --> 01:59:47,848
She drew our whole family.

1969
01:59:47,854 --> 01:59:50,032
- Look at the little dog, Paula, there.
- Oh, so cute.

1970
01:59:51,532 --> 01:59:54,033
..but, deep down we're...
we're all human,

1971
01:59:54,039 --> 01:59:56,040
we all miss our families, and...

1972
01:59:56,046 --> 01:59:57,799
we're doing it for them.

1973
01:59:58,111 --> 02:00:01,532
When a moment like this comes
along, and you see people

1974
02:00:01,538 --> 02:00:03,397
in this true light,

1975
02:00:03,403 --> 02:00:07,135
you know that none of this is
fake, none of this is bullshit,

1976
02:00:07,141 --> 02:00:09,578
it's just them and
their families, and...

1977
02:00:09,584 --> 02:00:13,371
..it's a touching moment to see
everyone go through that.

1978
02:00:13,377 --> 02:00:15,782
That's... that's my mum...

1979
02:00:15,788 --> 02:00:18,532
..when I was about 23.

1980
02:00:19,367 --> 02:00:21,533
When I made it into footy,

1981
02:00:21,539 --> 02:00:23,315
like, I was always tryin' to
get out of my dad's shadow,

1982
02:00:23,321 --> 02:00:25,630
and she said to me one day, she
goes, "You've made it, mate..."

1983
02:00:25,636 --> 02:00:26,782
..and I'm like, "What do you mean?"

1984
02:00:26,788 --> 02:00:30,032
She goes, "I'm no longer Steve
Rogers wife, I'm Mat Rogers mum."

1985
02:00:33,125 --> 02:00:38,532
And then, um... it changes,
just like that. Bang.

1986
02:00:39,458 --> 02:00:41,365
What's going on, mate?

1987
02:00:41,371 --> 02:00:42,746
What's the matter?

1988
02:00:43,498 --> 02:00:47,282
What's happened? What's
happened? What's happened?

1989
02:00:47,784 --> 02:00:50,782
What's happened? What's the matter?

1990
02:00:52,855 --> 02:00:56,720
Ah, Mum had a major stroke...

1991
02:00:56,726 --> 02:01:00,533
- Oh, are you serious?
- ..and, um...

1992
02:01:01,809 --> 02:01:04,649
- ..doesn't look like she's gonna make it.
- Oh god, Lee.

1993
02:01:06,269 --> 02:01:07,269
Sorry.

1994
02:01:07,841 --> 02:01:13,282
Lee just wanted to make his mum
proud and I'm sure he's done that.

1995
02:01:15,357 --> 02:01:19,032
Lee, for anyone that has
lost a parent, I mean...

1996
02:01:19,396 --> 02:01:21,281
..I can say, I can
only speak for myself,

1997
02:01:21,287 --> 02:01:23,398
like, I-I was with you in that moment.

1998
02:01:23,404 --> 02:01:26,788
I was, I know exactly what
it is to be that, and, um...

1999
02:01:26,914 --> 02:01:32,031
..it was really, really generous of you
to... to grieve so hon-honestly,

2000
02:01:32,037 --> 02:01:36,531
um, so that we could be there with
you, and feel that moment with you.

2001
02:01:36,537 --> 02:01:38,552
Your mum did end up passing away.

2002
02:01:38,558 --> 02:01:40,013
We are very, very sorry for your loss.

2003
02:01:40,019 --> 02:01:41,756
How are... how are you
and the family coping?

2004
02:01:41,762 --> 02:01:43,959
Yeah, we're good. We're...
we're working through it.

2005
02:01:43,965 --> 02:01:46,782
We're, sort of, six months
down the track now, but...

2006
02:01:47,047 --> 02:01:49,713
..you know, a situation like
that where you just get...

2007
02:01:49,950 --> 02:01:52,102
..you know, yeah, the
grieving process continues

2008
02:01:52,108 --> 02:01:54,006
and then you just get
thrown straight back into it,

2009
02:01:54,012 --> 02:01:57,782
and, you know, that'll never
be easy to watch, and...

2010
02:01:57,788 --> 02:01:59,718
..you know, what I can say, though,

2011
02:01:59,827 --> 02:02:04,044
the people around me, that just, the
game stopped, and everyone just...

2012
02:02:04,187 --> 02:02:07,532
..rallied around me, not
only my tribe mates,

2013
02:02:07,538 --> 02:02:10,686
um, but production and everyone.

2014
02:02:10,692 --> 02:02:13,032
and that just is a testament
to the game and to the people.

2015
02:02:13,038 --> 02:02:16,427
You know, we're all out there,
we're doing it for our family,

2016
02:02:16,433 --> 02:02:18,032
um, and for ourselves,

2017
02:02:18,038 --> 02:02:20,713
and, you know, for something like
that to happen is the worst thing

2018
02:02:20,719 --> 02:02:23,910
because you've so far
away from home, and, um,

2019
02:02:23,916 --> 02:02:27,032
forever I will be grateful for...

2020
02:02:29,782 --> 02:02:32,283
..the people around, um,

2021
02:02:32,289 --> 02:02:34,794
especially Tarzy, um...

2022
02:02:35,532 --> 02:02:38,264
..to get me through that... that time.

2023
02:02:39,282 --> 02:02:40,722
Tarzan...

2024
02:02:40,728 --> 02:02:43,786
- ..how would you describe that
afternoon in camp? - Yeah.

2025
02:02:44,564 --> 02:02:48,207
You know, I was just, I was just
happy to be there for Lee, you know.

2026
02:02:48,213 --> 02:02:49,537
It was, um...

2027
02:02:50,032 --> 02:02:53,143
Everyone plays a role
in this game, and...

2028
02:02:53,149 --> 02:02:55,786
..as everyone has said,
what they do, and...

2029
02:02:55,792 --> 02:02:58,282
well, I was just happy
to be there for Lee.

2030
02:02:58,887 --> 02:03:00,687
- That's it, that's it.
- Well,

2031
02:03:00,693 --> 02:03:04,122
Lee that episode resulted in a huge
outpouring of.. of support.

2032
02:03:04,128 --> 02:03:06,971
Have you manage to channel
that positivity somewhere?

2033
02:03:06,977 --> 02:03:10,653
We have. We, uh, decided to do something
good out of... out of tragedy,

2034
02:03:10,659 --> 02:03:13,587
and, um, you know, through the
Stroke Foundation, uh...

2035
02:03:13,728 --> 02:03:16,259
Dave and I have worked pretty hard
through the little Towel Challenge

2036
02:03:16,265 --> 02:03:18,225
and, uh, that's going gang
busters at the moment.

2037
02:03:18,231 --> 02:03:20,323
Uh, we might have to
call you out, Osh. Uh...

2038
02:03:20,329 --> 02:03:22,032
I think... I think we already did.

2039
02:03:22,038 --> 02:03:24,799
- We already did call you out, Osher.
- Yeah, you did already call me out.

2040
02:03:24,805 --> 02:03:27,336
- Are we waiting on that? Is that
happening? - Oh, lost my phone.

2041
02:03:27,342 --> 02:03:28,895
Sorry to put you on the spot, mate.

2042
02:03:28,920 --> 02:03:31,181
Ah, that's good. Well, you know,
we've raised a lot of money,

2043
02:03:31,187 --> 02:03:33,944
but more importantly, uh, we've
raised heaps of awareness

2044
02:03:33,950 --> 02:03:36,222
You know, 1 in 4 people will
have a stroke in their life,

2045
02:03:36,228 --> 02:03:39,132
and these are numbers, these
are bad stats, and...

2046
02:03:39,138 --> 02:03:41,598
um, as I said, we're just
trying to do something good,

2047
02:03:41,604 --> 02:03:44,782
and... out of something
really tragic, and, um,

2048
02:03:44,788 --> 02:03:47,036
yeah, I can't thank, again,
the Survivor community,

2049
02:03:47,042 --> 02:03:50,066
especially David, enough.
For him to reach out, um...

2050
02:03:50,072 --> 02:03:52,460
meant so much to me to...
to get this off the ground

2051
02:03:52,473 --> 02:03:55,410
and, ah, you know, when... when
David talks people listen,

2052
02:03:55,416 --> 02:03:57,784
and, uh, it's been going
really well at the moment.

2053
02:03:59,408 --> 02:04:01,019
I couldn't have said it better.

2054
02:04:01,025 --> 02:04:02,851
Well, clearly leaving

2055
02:04:02,857 --> 02:04:06,282
friends and family behind to
play this game is tough, so...

2056
02:04:06,288 --> 02:04:09,993
you really have to make your
time on Survivor count.

2057
02:04:09,999 --> 02:04:14,782
After the break we find out if everyone
here got the All Stars revenge

2058
02:04:14,788 --> 02:04:16,034
that they came for.

2059
02:04:27,812 --> 02:04:32,032
All Stars Reunion Show and...

2060
02:04:32,038 --> 02:04:34,752
with a cast made up of returning players

2061
02:04:34,758 --> 02:04:39,038
there were bound to be a few old
scores that needed to be settled.

2062
02:04:40,022 --> 02:04:44,032
I was the reason why Lydia
was voted out of the game.

2063
02:04:49,195 --> 02:04:54,032
I'm super excited that I can
take out my revenge on Shane.

2064
02:04:54,038 --> 02:04:55,287
I want her out.

2065
02:04:57,405 --> 02:05:02,032
First person voted out of
Australian Survivor: All Stars... Shane.

2066
02:05:02,992 --> 02:05:05,782
- It's the first time I've done this.
- Oh, yeah, you've never done this.

2067
02:05:05,807 --> 02:05:07,547
First time for everything.

2068
02:05:21,421 --> 02:05:25,031
The Cookie Monster's going down
without even getting one cookie.

2069
02:05:25,037 --> 02:05:27,282
I think there's some irony
in that, don't you think?

2070
02:05:28,664 --> 02:05:32,132
Thing is, not a fan of the old Daisy...

2071
02:05:32,468 --> 02:05:35,132
..just because of what she did
to me last time we played.

2072
02:05:35,235 --> 02:05:37,450
She blindsided me!

2073
02:05:37,456 --> 02:05:39,782
Oh, naughty, naughty.

2074
02:05:39,788 --> 02:05:41,275
It's revenge time.

2075
02:05:41,281 --> 02:05:44,505
Third person voted out of
Australian Survivor: All Stars...

2076
02:05:45,349 --> 02:05:47,428
..Daisy. Need to
bring me your torch.

2077
02:05:48,286 --> 02:05:50,380
At least we've worked together before...

2078
02:05:50,386 --> 02:05:52,807
- Yeah. We know how each other works.
- ..d'you know what I mean? Like, we...

2079
02:05:52,813 --> 02:05:54,791
I know how... what you're
like when you lie now.

2080
02:05:56,492 --> 02:05:59,031
The last time I played
Flick told me to my face

2081
02:05:59,037 --> 02:06:01,287
she was with me, 100
percent, to the end,

2082
02:06:01,626 --> 02:06:03,532
probably the day she voted me out.

2083
02:06:04,341 --> 02:06:06,032
I came here to make big moves

2084
02:06:06,038 --> 02:06:09,307
and get revenge on someone who
completely destroyed my game.

2085
02:06:09,313 --> 02:06:11,675
Brooke, now what?

2086
02:06:11,976 --> 02:06:14,783
Now we've gotta turn on
our own, unfortunately.

2087
02:06:14,789 --> 02:06:19,282
11th person voted out of
Australian Survivor: All Stars, Flick.

2088
02:06:24,288 --> 02:06:28,537
I actually gotta go, uh,
something's come up.

2089
02:06:28,543 --> 02:06:30,670
- Brooke, you waited four years to take out
- Yeah.

2090
02:06:30,676 --> 02:06:33,725
- your revenge on Flick...
- I did.

2091
02:06:33,731 --> 02:06:36,532
..how did it feel to finally
write her name down?

2092
02:06:36,538 --> 02:06:39,424
- Oh, it felt... it felt...
- Just say it felt good.

2093
02:06:39,723 --> 02:06:43,037
I'm gonna, like, not gonna beat
around the bush, it felt bloody good.

2094
02:06:43,043 --> 02:06:46,866
One goal for me was, "Make sure
you get her before she gets you",

2095
02:06:46,872 --> 02:06:49,532
and that's just been in my
head for a while, so...

2096
02:06:49,538 --> 02:06:51,921
..yeah, it did feel
good, but, I am, I do,

2097
02:06:51,927 --> 02:06:53,878
- I am sorry. I love you.
- I love you, too.

2098
02:06:55,266 --> 02:06:58,306
Flick, did you expect that Brooke
would try and take you out?

2099
02:06:58,312 --> 02:07:01,201
- Yeah, definitely, I did expect it.
- I mean this is All Stars.

2100
02:07:01,207 --> 02:07:03,282
I knew Brooke was coming
after me at some point.

2101
02:07:03,288 --> 02:07:07,480
Um, unfortunately I couldn't get
to her, I couldn't get the numbers,

2102
02:07:07,486 --> 02:07:11,338
um, and look, for her,
that was a great move.

2103
02:07:11,344 --> 02:07:13,743
I was a big threat to her game,

2104
02:07:13,749 --> 02:07:17,894
I blindsided her in Season
One, and, yeah, she... she

2105
02:07:17,900 --> 02:07:19,780
made an amazing choice to get rid of me

2106
02:07:19,786 --> 02:07:22,431
so I don't have any ill
feelings towards her,

2107
02:07:22,437 --> 02:07:24,961
and I think it was a... a great
move for Brooke to make.

2108
02:07:25,214 --> 02:07:29,559
David, you ended up with the
title, congratulations.

2109
02:07:29,565 --> 02:07:33,532
What was it like to play this incredible
game with 23 other All Stars?

2110
02:07:33,794 --> 02:07:38,239
Ah, phew, I... it's... that's very
hard to explain. I think, um,

2111
02:07:38,245 --> 02:07:39,810
it was just a rollercoaster ride,

2112
02:07:39,816 --> 02:07:42,125
and as you're on it you think
some things are working,

2113
02:07:42,131 --> 02:07:43,592
some things are not working,

2114
02:07:43,598 --> 02:07:47,130
and we were playing at what I
felt like was such a high level

2115
02:07:47,136 --> 02:07:49,533
that... it was... it
was just really hard,

2116
02:07:49,546 --> 02:07:52,282
but to know I was going
up against the best

2117
02:07:52,288 --> 02:07:54,282
and still end up with the title is,

2118
02:07:54,288 --> 02:07:57,002
uh, is pretty... pretty
flattering, I think.

2119
02:07:57,316 --> 02:07:59,781
Well, All Stars has been a season

2120
02:07:59,787 --> 02:08:02,728
that most definitely lived up to
it's name in every single way,

2121
02:08:02,734 --> 02:08:03,968
As a fan of the show,

2122
02:08:03,974 --> 02:08:06,548
thank you all so very much for
putting your lives on hold,

2123
02:08:06,554 --> 02:08:08,837
going to the other side of the world
to play this incredible game.

2124
02:08:08,843 --> 02:08:10,969
It was magnificent to watch every night.

2125
02:08:11,111 --> 02:08:14,281
That is it for this season of
Australian Survivor: All Stars.

2126
02:08:14,287 --> 02:08:18,334
Thank you so much for joining us.
Between now and next season

2127
02:08:18,340 --> 02:08:20,531
make sure you look after your tribe,

2128
02:08:20,537 --> 02:08:23,504
and remember that in the end we
really are all in this tribe together.

2129
02:08:23,510 --> 02:08:25,327
Thanks for watching,
good night, Australia.

2130
02:08:26,609 --> 02:08:29,324
subs ripped from air, thanks for
Peta for providing

2131
02:08:29,355 --> 02:08:31,819
and transcribing the end that
didn't record

2132
02:08:31,843 --> 02:08:34,742
timing:
dom.smrc



## S08E24

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,162
WWW.MY-SUBS.CO

1
00:00:01,667 --> 00:00:04,146
The harsh Australian outback...

2
00:00:05,667 --> 00:00:08,226
..home to a new breed of player.

3
00:00:09,266 --> 00:00:10,266
Brains...

4
00:00:10,267 --> 00:00:12,546
You don't
need big muscles to fight.

5
00:00:12,587 --> 00:00:15,066
The strongest muscle is the brain.

6
00:00:15,107 --> 00:00:16,666
..versus brawn.

7
00:00:16,707 --> 00:00:20,906
The gladiator style of
competing, it's in my blood.

8
00:00:20,947 --> 00:00:24,306
Go, go, go, go, go! Let's go!

9
00:00:25,347 --> 00:00:26,866
Here to outwit...

10
00:00:26,907 --> 00:00:28,426
Go, go, go!

11
00:00:28,467 --> 00:00:30,186
- Well done!
- Give it everything!

12
00:00:30,227 --> 00:00:31,626
..outplay...

13
00:00:31,667 --> 00:00:33,186
Come on, Survivors! Push it!

14
00:00:34,347 --> 00:00:35,626
- ..and...
- Go!

15
00:00:35,667 --> 00:00:36,946
..outlast.

16
00:00:36,987 --> 00:00:39,746
- Oh!
- Come on!

17
00:00:39,787 --> 00:00:41,306
For 48 days...

18
00:00:44,467 --> 00:00:45,586
I am the puppet master.

19
00:00:45,627 --> 00:00:46,627
Bring it on, baby.

20
00:00:46,667 --> 00:00:48,666
Game on, moll!

21
00:00:48,707 --> 00:00:50,786
..through the most loyal alliances...

22
00:00:50,827 --> 00:00:52,986
My guardian angel is here!

23
00:00:53,027 --> 00:00:54,866
It's Big D's time.

24
00:00:54,907 --> 00:00:56,426
Spicy baby!

25
00:00:56,467 --> 00:00:58,306
- ..and...
- I have two idols.

26
00:00:58,347 --> 00:01:00,306
..spectacular blindsides.

27
00:01:00,347 --> 00:01:03,146
I am unstoppable.

28
00:01:03,187 --> 00:01:04,506
Simon.

29
00:01:04,547 --> 00:01:05,746
- Did you know it was coming?
- Yep.

30
00:01:05,787 --> 00:01:06,787
Laura.

31
00:01:07,827 --> 00:01:08,906
What?!

32
00:01:08,947 --> 00:01:10,506
Emmett.

33
00:01:10,547 --> 00:01:13,506
One by one, they were voted out.

34
00:01:15,387 --> 00:01:16,906
For reals.

35
00:01:16,947 --> 00:01:19,826
And now just three remain.

36
00:01:21,187 --> 00:01:22,506
George.

37
00:01:22,547 --> 00:01:25,066
I came here to raise the bar.

38
00:01:25,107 --> 00:01:28,546
It doesn't matter how much it
hurts, I'm gonna get that crown.

39
00:01:29,587 --> 00:01:30,826
Hayley.

40
00:01:30,867 --> 00:01:33,626
You have to believe in
yourself. You have to be strong.

41
00:01:33,667 --> 00:01:36,026
I have been preparing
for this my whole life.

42
00:01:36,067 --> 00:01:38,226
I have pushed so hard

43
00:01:38,267 --> 00:01:42,066
and I am ready to take
out the title of Sole Survivor.

44
00:01:42,107 --> 00:01:43,226
Flick.

45
00:01:43,267 --> 00:01:47,146
I'm fearless, I'm
courageous and I'm so brave.

46
00:01:47,187 --> 00:01:51,306
I've sacrificed so much
and I'm not giving up now.

47
00:01:51,347 --> 00:01:55,946
Tonight, one will be
crowned Sole Survivor.

48
00:02:45,027 --> 00:02:49,186
It's day 47 and
I've made the final three.

49
00:02:50,267 --> 00:02:52,306
And to think that I've outlasted

50
00:02:52,347 --> 00:02:56,666
21 other Survivor contestants is insane.

51
00:02:59,227 --> 00:03:01,186
But here I am

52
00:03:01,227 --> 00:03:04,066
and I'm proud to represent
the last Brawn standing.

53
00:03:05,707 --> 00:03:08,746
My physical game has
been incredibly strong,

54
00:03:08,787 --> 00:03:11,026
but I've played a great social game.

55
00:03:11,067 --> 00:03:15,346
I have really relied on making
genuine connections with people

56
00:03:15,387 --> 00:03:16,986
and I pride myself on that.

57
00:03:18,387 --> 00:03:22,386
But when I think back to
my experience out here,

58
00:03:22,427 --> 00:03:27,106
I think my journey has been
very different to everyone else's.

59
00:03:30,947 --> 00:03:32,866
I came in here knowing that

60
00:03:32,907 --> 00:03:35,466
I would pride myself
on my physical abilities,

61
00:03:35,507 --> 00:03:38,266
never backing down from a challenge,

62
00:03:38,307 --> 00:03:41,626
putting my body on the line,
and I know I definitely did that,

63
00:03:41,667 --> 00:03:45,786
but I think the real
strength for me out here

64
00:03:45,827 --> 00:03:47,466
was definitely my mental strength.

65
00:03:49,387 --> 00:03:51,546
There's been so many points in this game

66
00:03:51,587 --> 00:03:54,866
where I have been at breaking point,

67
00:03:54,907 --> 00:03:57,946
but I know that my mum
would have wanted me to stay...

68
00:03:59,587 --> 00:04:03,266
..and that's what I've drawn on

69
00:04:03,307 --> 00:04:06,546
as inspiration to keep
going in the game.

70
00:04:06,587 --> 00:04:10,146
I have come up against
the hardest circumstances

71
00:04:10,187 --> 00:04:12,786
and I'm still here
and I'm still fighting.

72
00:04:12,827 --> 00:04:16,666
And knowing that drives
me even harder to win today.

73
00:04:20,147 --> 00:04:23,386
For the past two weeks here
I've been fighting for my life

74
00:04:23,427 --> 00:04:25,386
and it hasn't been easy.

75
00:04:25,427 --> 00:04:28,066
But we've been out here for 47 days

76
00:04:28,107 --> 00:04:32,546
and the winner will be
crowned in less than 48 hours.

77
00:04:33,827 --> 00:04:37,586
And if I have the
opportunity to pitch to the jury,

78
00:04:37,627 --> 00:04:39,666
I feel like I would have their vote.

79
00:04:41,067 --> 00:04:43,466
I'm definitely ready to
put my body on the line,

80
00:04:43,507 --> 00:04:45,986
to fight to get all the way to the end.

81
00:04:57,707 --> 00:04:59,626
I've had a plan since day one -

82
00:04:59,667 --> 00:05:02,106
it's to be a smooth political operative

83
00:05:02,147 --> 00:05:04,746
running a well-oiled campaign.

84
00:05:06,107 --> 00:05:07,706
And that's what I've done.

85
00:05:07,747 --> 00:05:11,226
Gathered cold, hard facts,

86
00:05:11,267 --> 00:05:13,226
campaigned for votes.

87
00:05:14,547 --> 00:05:16,186
And, more importantly,

88
00:05:16,227 --> 00:05:20,026
I've always been one step
ahead of the opposition.

89
00:05:21,867 --> 00:05:25,626
People might think I've gotten
lucky, but I didn't get lucky.

90
00:05:25,667 --> 00:05:29,346
I worked hard to pull
myself from the bottom

91
00:05:29,387 --> 00:05:33,586
and shake the target off
my back every single day.

92
00:05:34,627 --> 00:05:37,986
What I've proven is
that a man with a plan

93
00:05:38,027 --> 00:05:40,706
and a big brain like myself

94
00:05:40,747 --> 00:05:45,986
can outlast a whole heap of
muscle and brawn to succeed.

95
00:05:47,907 --> 00:05:49,986
I have physical limitations,

96
00:05:50,027 --> 00:05:53,306
but I'm not gonna let
that be my downfall.

97
00:05:53,347 --> 00:05:56,506
I might not have won a
single immunity challenge,

98
00:05:56,547 --> 00:06:01,346
but the final challenge is
the only one that matters.

99
00:06:01,387 --> 00:06:04,106
I am really determined to win today.

100
00:06:05,147 --> 00:06:07,266
If it's me in that final two,

101
00:06:07,307 --> 00:06:10,466
I'm in the box seat to
win half a million dollars

102
00:06:10,507 --> 00:06:13,466
and get that crown that
I so rightfully deserve.

103
00:06:13,507 --> 00:06:15,026
But if I lose,

104
00:06:15,067 --> 00:06:18,866
Hayley or Flick take
the power away from me.

105
00:06:18,907 --> 00:06:21,346
I'm not gonna give up
at today's challenge.

106
00:06:22,387 --> 00:06:24,226
It doesn't matter how much it hurts.

107
00:06:24,267 --> 00:06:27,266
I need to get to Election Day,

108
00:06:27,307 --> 00:06:28,826
and that's tomorrow.

109
00:06:28,867 --> 00:06:30,786
So I'm gonna grit my teeth

110
00:06:30,827 --> 00:06:32,266
and I'm gonna get the job done.

111
00:06:33,627 --> 00:06:35,826
My campaign and fight isn't over.

112
00:06:44,107 --> 00:06:47,746
It is an absolute
dream come true to play this game.

113
00:06:49,467 --> 00:06:51,946
I started watching this
game 20 years ago.

114
00:06:52,987 --> 00:06:56,186
I have been researching and
preparing for this moment my whole life.

115
00:06:57,187 --> 00:06:59,146
And now I'm here.

116
00:06:59,187 --> 00:07:02,506
I have a one-in-three shot
of being the Sole Survivor.

117
00:07:02,547 --> 00:07:05,506
It is unbelievable to
think about. I pinch myself.

118
00:07:10,587 --> 00:07:13,266
Now there are only two
people left to get past.

119
00:07:13,307 --> 00:07:15,746
But my competition is fierce.

120
00:07:17,627 --> 00:07:21,026
King George is the epitome of Brains,

121
00:07:21,067 --> 00:07:23,986
and he's played almost
the perfect strategic game.

122
00:07:25,107 --> 00:07:27,826
Flick has been the
ultimate Brawn out here.

123
00:07:27,867 --> 00:07:30,386
She has been a huge physical contender

124
00:07:30,427 --> 00:07:32,986
and built amazing social connections.

125
00:07:34,027 --> 00:07:36,066
But what they don't know

126
00:07:36,107 --> 00:07:39,706
is that I'm the perfect
mix of brain and brawn.

127
00:07:39,747 --> 00:07:41,626
That's a dangerous combination.

128
00:07:44,427 --> 00:07:46,306
This final immunity challenge

129
00:07:46,347 --> 00:07:48,586
is the most important challenge

130
00:07:48,627 --> 00:07:52,586
because it secures you
a spot in the final two

131
00:07:52,627 --> 00:07:56,386
and gives you all the power
to decide who you sit next to.

132
00:07:56,427 --> 00:07:58,346
It could be the make or break

133
00:07:58,387 --> 00:08:00,546
between you and half a million dollars.

134
00:08:00,587 --> 00:08:02,546
Come on in, guys!

135
00:08:04,987 --> 00:08:07,306
In the real world, I research pain.

136
00:08:07,347 --> 00:08:09,426
I've been studying pain for years,

137
00:08:09,467 --> 00:08:12,626
so I know what it
takes to overcome pain.

138
00:08:12,667 --> 00:08:15,946
I know how to push myself to
the edge and how to get past that.

139
00:08:16,987 --> 00:08:21,306
And I'm willing to use all of that
knowledge to help me win today.

140
00:08:21,347 --> 00:08:23,026
Oh, my God.

141
00:08:39,787 --> 00:08:42,186
That looks like torture.

142
00:08:45,587 --> 00:08:47,106
Well, congratulations, guys.

143
00:08:47,147 --> 00:08:50,186
You made it to day 47.

144
00:08:51,947 --> 00:08:53,946
You've endured gruelling conditions

145
00:08:53,987 --> 00:08:58,946
and you've outlasted 21
other people to get this far.

146
00:08:58,987 --> 00:09:00,386
Well done.

147
00:09:00,427 --> 00:09:04,466
Now, are you ready to get to
your final immunity challenge?

148
00:09:04,507 --> 00:09:06,466
- Yes!
- Yes.

149
00:09:06,507 --> 00:09:08,786
Flick, I'm gonna need it back.

150
00:09:08,827 --> 00:09:09,946
Argh!

151
00:09:09,987 --> 00:09:11,386
It'll be coming back soon.

152
00:09:17,267 --> 00:09:21,586
For the last time, immunity
is back up for grabs.

153
00:09:23,867 --> 00:09:25,226
For today's challenge...

154
00:09:26,987 --> 00:09:29,266
..you'll each step into a chamber

155
00:09:29,307 --> 00:09:32,186
standing on very
narrow pegs on the floor

156
00:09:32,227 --> 00:09:35,666
while holding on to
spikes on the ceiling.

157
00:09:36,707 --> 00:09:38,866
At regular intervals,
the ceiling will drop...

158
00:09:40,027 --> 00:09:43,226
..making it more difficult
for you to hold that position.

159
00:09:43,267 --> 00:09:48,146
If at any point you fall
off the pegs or step off,

160
00:09:48,187 --> 00:09:49,666
you're out of the challenge.

161
00:09:51,787 --> 00:09:54,546
Last person standing wins immunity

162
00:09:54,587 --> 00:09:58,026
and a guaranteed spot
at that final tribal council

163
00:09:58,067 --> 00:10:00,706
where you'll have the
chance to pitch to the jury

164
00:10:00,747 --> 00:10:04,306
why you deserve the
title of Sole Survivor

165
00:10:04,347 --> 00:10:06,026
and the half million
dollars that goes with it.

166
00:10:07,227 --> 00:10:09,106
Plus, you'll get to decide

167
00:10:09,147 --> 00:10:12,466
who will be sitting next
to you at that tribal council.

168
00:10:14,787 --> 00:10:17,026
Now, this is a tough challenge,

169
00:10:17,067 --> 00:10:18,746
there's a lot on the line,

170
00:10:18,787 --> 00:10:23,186
so we figured that you might
need a little extra love from home...

171
00:10:24,707 --> 00:10:26,226
..to help you through this.

172
00:10:31,707 --> 00:10:34,266
- Hayley, you ready for this?
- Yeah.

173
00:10:34,307 --> 00:10:36,386
Come on in, guys!

174
00:10:42,307 --> 00:10:44,746
Yes.

175
00:11:03,187 --> 00:11:05,306
Katie.

176
00:11:13,027 --> 00:11:14,066
OK, so, Hayley...

177
00:11:14,107 --> 00:11:16,346
So I know their names,
but who are they to you?

178
00:11:16,387 --> 00:11:20,506
This is Jimmy, my boyfriend,
and Kate, my best mate.

179
00:11:20,547 --> 00:11:24,986
So, how does it feel to
see Jimmy after 47 days?

180
00:11:25,027 --> 00:11:26,666
Oh, my God. It feels so good.

181
00:11:26,707 --> 00:11:31,026
It's just weird for them to be like
actually here and can touch them.

182
00:11:31,067 --> 00:11:32,706
It's so good. It's so nice.

183
00:11:32,747 --> 00:11:35,426
Jimmy, are you surprised
that Hayley is still here?

184
00:11:35,467 --> 00:11:37,626
Yes and no.

185
00:11:37,667 --> 00:11:41,226
She's absolutely amazing
and incredible and so strong

186
00:11:41,267 --> 00:11:45,586
and, oh... I'm just, like, so amazed.

187
00:11:45,627 --> 00:11:49,026
Hayley, those are all
the correct answers, right?

188
00:11:49,067 --> 00:11:50,986
Yeah. Keep saying nice things.

189
00:11:51,027 --> 00:11:53,466
What would it mean to
Hayley to win this game?

190
00:11:53,507 --> 00:11:57,546
Oh, it would be... it
would be life-changing.

191
00:11:57,587 --> 00:12:00,386
She's already done so amazing.

192
00:12:00,427 --> 00:12:04,346
So anything beyond this
is just an absolute bonus.

193
00:12:07,347 --> 00:12:09,266
- So, George.
- Yes.

194
00:12:09,307 --> 00:12:11,746
Who is it that you'd love to see today?

195
00:12:11,787 --> 00:12:13,786
I've really been missing my mum.

196
00:12:15,347 --> 00:12:19,426
It's just kind of been building,
so, hopefully she's there.

197
00:12:19,467 --> 00:12:21,346
Well, let's find out.

198
00:12:21,387 --> 00:12:22,506
Come on in, guys.

199
00:12:29,507 --> 00:12:32,066
Oh, my God.

200
00:12:42,507 --> 00:12:45,066
I'm so close.

201
00:12:45,107 --> 00:12:47,506
Hello. Hi.

202
00:12:52,667 --> 00:12:56,466
Look at you. Look at you.

203
00:12:56,507 --> 00:12:58,826
Alright, George, can you
give me an introduction?

204
00:12:58,867 --> 00:13:02,186
This is my mum, Maria,
and this is my sister, Pamela.

205
00:13:02,227 --> 00:13:03,906
- OK.
- Yeah.

206
00:13:03,947 --> 00:13:05,386
- So, Maria.
- Yes.

207
00:13:05,427 --> 00:13:08,426
When George came to you and said,
"Mum, I'm going to go play Survivor,"

208
00:13:08,467 --> 00:13:09,906
what did you think?

209
00:13:09,947 --> 00:13:11,586
I wasn't that surprised,

210
00:13:11,627 --> 00:13:15,466
because I know once he puts his
mind to anything, he can do whatever.

211
00:13:15,507 --> 00:13:19,586
Day one he stood in front
of me in his bowling whites.

212
00:13:20,667 --> 00:13:23,106
They're bowling dirty browns now.

213
00:13:23,147 --> 00:13:25,226
You're going to have to
wash them in a few days.

214
00:13:25,267 --> 00:13:28,146
That's fine. That's fine. I
look forward to doing that.

215
00:13:28,187 --> 00:13:30,426
So, George, how much
have you missed your mother?

216
00:13:30,467 --> 00:13:33,706
I have missed my mother.

217
00:13:33,747 --> 00:13:35,986
Whilst I'm physically depleted,

218
00:13:36,027 --> 00:13:38,266
I'm here for you guys, so...

219
00:13:38,307 --> 00:13:40,026
And we're here for you.

220
00:13:46,027 --> 00:13:47,466
Flick.

221
00:13:52,627 --> 00:13:54,306
Yes.

222
00:13:54,347 --> 00:13:56,306
I know this game has been
especially tough for you.

223
00:13:56,347 --> 00:13:59,026
- So let's get you some love.
- Yeah.

224
00:14:00,427 --> 00:14:01,746
Oh...

225
00:14:37,107 --> 00:14:39,666
It's so good to see you.

226
00:14:56,507 --> 00:14:59,026
It's hard to keep it together.

227
00:14:59,067 --> 00:15:00,306
That's alright.

228
00:15:00,347 --> 00:15:02,066
It's really hard to keep it together.

229
00:15:12,787 --> 00:15:14,626
Alright, Flick, who do you have here?

230
00:15:14,667 --> 00:15:17,306
Oh, I have my beautiful partner, Mitch.

231
00:15:17,347 --> 00:15:20,106
Who I haven't seen in
four and a half months.

232
00:15:20,147 --> 00:15:23,746
So it's amazing to see him.

233
00:15:23,787 --> 00:15:27,426
My beautiful best friend who I've
been friends with for over 20 years.

234
00:15:27,467 --> 00:15:31,106
What does it mean to have
these guys here with you today?

235
00:15:34,627 --> 00:15:37,586
Words can't describe for me right now.

236
00:15:37,627 --> 00:15:41,266
Like, it's hard enough being
out here away from your family

237
00:15:41,307 --> 00:15:44,746
and losing my mum while I've been here.

238
00:15:46,067 --> 00:15:50,746
And all I wanted is the
people I'm closest to,

239
00:15:50,787 --> 00:15:54,266
for support, and not having
that has been incredibly tough.

240
00:15:54,307 --> 00:15:57,346
So...

241
00:15:57,387 --> 00:16:00,306
..just to see their faces.

242
00:16:00,347 --> 00:16:04,146
Oh, I couldn't ask for
anything more. I really couldn't.

243
00:16:06,587 --> 00:16:13,666
Mitch, after 47 days, Flick
is still here, still fighting.

244
00:16:13,707 --> 00:16:15,346
Does that surprise you?

245
00:16:15,387 --> 00:16:18,466
Not at all. No. She's amazing.

246
00:16:18,507 --> 00:16:21,946
I would have been surprised
if she didn't get this far, so...

247
00:16:21,987 --> 00:16:23,866
She's just... just incredible.

248
00:16:23,907 --> 00:16:26,706
So, so proud of her. Yeah.

249
00:16:26,747 --> 00:16:30,346
She's the strongest
person I know, by far.

250
00:16:30,387 --> 00:16:31,626
Very strong.

251
00:16:33,987 --> 00:16:38,426
OK, loved ones, you guys are going
to be cheering on from the bench today.

252
00:16:38,467 --> 00:16:42,866
Hayley, Flick, George,

253
00:16:42,907 --> 00:16:44,866
we're going to get to it.

254
00:16:44,907 --> 00:16:47,066
- I'll just hug you.
- Yes.

255
00:16:47,107 --> 00:16:49,066
I'd forgotten how tall you were.

256
00:16:50,867 --> 00:16:53,506
Oh...

257
00:16:53,547 --> 00:16:55,866
This is the time to do it, George.

258
00:17:21,347 --> 00:17:25,506
Alright, guys, let's
step up into position.

259
00:17:38,867 --> 00:17:41,186
Alright.

260
00:17:41,227 --> 00:17:43,186
Final immunity.

261
00:17:46,387 --> 00:17:47,906
This challenge...

262
00:17:49,547 --> 00:17:51,306
..is now on.

263
00:17:54,867 --> 00:17:59,106
So here we are, we're
down to two Brains...

264
00:18:00,707 --> 00:18:02,986
..one Brawn.

265
00:18:03,027 --> 00:18:04,986
All you gotta do

266
00:18:05,027 --> 00:18:07,746
is outlast two other people,

267
00:18:07,787 --> 00:18:10,466
and you will have a chance

268
00:18:10,507 --> 00:18:12,746
to pitch to the jury,

269
00:18:12,787 --> 00:18:15,226
a shot at that half million dollars.

270
00:18:15,267 --> 00:18:18,986
You could move around that bed of nails.

271
00:18:19,027 --> 00:18:21,626
Left to right.

272
00:18:21,667 --> 00:18:23,386
Front to back.

273
00:18:23,427 --> 00:18:26,946
At some stage,

274
00:18:26,987 --> 00:18:28,786
I'm going to lower that ceiling.

275
00:18:31,667 --> 00:18:34,826
Making it more difficult
to hold your position.

276
00:18:36,947 --> 00:18:39,546
Fall or step off the pegs...

277
00:18:41,427 --> 00:18:43,626
..you're out of the challenge.

278
00:18:43,667 --> 00:18:44,946
No pressure.

279
00:18:57,307 --> 00:18:59,866
15 minutes into this challenge.

280
00:18:59,907 --> 00:19:01,666
George, how are you feeling?

281
00:19:01,707 --> 00:19:04,986
Well, I'm glad I lasted more
than four minutes today.

282
00:19:05,027 --> 00:19:07,746
Yeah, me too.

283
00:19:07,787 --> 00:19:10,586
I've been waiting 47
days for my turn to do it!

284
00:19:10,627 --> 00:19:12,226
Let me win!

285
00:19:15,507 --> 00:19:17,506
So, you gonna let me win, Flick?

286
00:19:17,547 --> 00:19:19,306
No, I need this.

287
00:19:21,067 --> 00:19:23,666
I don't think I'm going
to final two if I don't.

288
00:19:40,667 --> 00:19:43,626
You guys been up there for 30 minutes.

289
00:19:45,347 --> 00:19:49,466
So, that position
was pretty easy, right?

290
00:19:51,907 --> 00:19:54,546
I think it's time to make
it a little more interesting.

291
00:19:54,587 --> 00:19:57,146
- Uh-huh.
- Oh.

292
00:19:58,507 --> 00:20:00,506
On the count of three,

293
00:20:00,547 --> 00:20:03,986
I'm going to lower that ceiling.

294
00:20:05,787 --> 00:20:06,946
Oh, wow.

295
00:20:06,987 --> 00:20:08,986
Here we go.

296
00:20:09,027 --> 00:20:10,746
Three...

297
00:20:13,267 --> 00:20:14,267
..two...

298
00:20:16,907 --> 00:20:18,266
..one.

299
00:20:27,787 --> 00:20:29,186
Oh, my God.

300
00:20:29,227 --> 00:20:30,626
Oh, shit.

301
00:20:44,503 --> 00:20:45,782
On the count of three...

302
00:20:47,223 --> 00:20:49,382
..I'm gonna lower that ceiling.

303
00:20:52,503 --> 00:20:55,942
Three, two...

304
00:20:56,983 --> 00:20:58,382
..one.

305
00:21:13,463 --> 00:21:15,662
Impossible to stand up straight now.

306
00:21:17,463 --> 00:21:20,142
Without your head
bumping into those spikes.

307
00:21:25,223 --> 00:21:27,742
Everyone's got a slightly different take

308
00:21:27,783 --> 00:21:30,182
on how to deal with this new position.

309
00:21:32,223 --> 00:21:36,982
Flick squatting down,
stretching her arms out.

310
00:21:37,023 --> 00:21:39,262
George leaning forward.

311
00:21:40,343 --> 00:21:41,862
Tippy-toes, eh?

312
00:21:41,903 --> 00:21:46,182
Hayley on those ballerina points.

313
00:21:50,623 --> 00:21:54,462
Those pedestals are gonna start
grinding into the soles of your feet.

314
00:21:56,303 --> 00:21:58,822
Like hundreds of tiny knives.

315
00:22:00,943 --> 00:22:03,942
The pain is only
increasing at this point.

316
00:22:07,743 --> 00:22:10,622
Every time you move your hands,
every time you make an adjustment...

317
00:22:11,703 --> 00:22:13,862
..you risk slipping off.

318
00:22:16,943 --> 00:22:21,102
Just tiny adjustments,
that's all you can make.

319
00:22:26,663 --> 00:22:28,142
I'm joking.

320
00:22:41,743 --> 00:22:43,702
Fresh dust in the afternoon.

321
00:22:48,383 --> 00:22:50,382
I love a bit of dust in the eyeballs.

322
00:22:52,023 --> 00:22:53,982
Flick, why are you smiling?

323
00:22:54,023 --> 00:22:56,582
Oh... I just find it funny.

324
00:22:56,623 --> 00:22:59,302
Like, why am I doing this to myself?

325
00:23:00,623 --> 00:23:03,182
So, why are you doing this, Flick?

326
00:23:03,223 --> 00:23:07,062
I am doing this for my family.

327
00:23:08,663 --> 00:23:10,582
They are my biggest inspiration.

328
00:23:10,623 --> 00:23:12,342
I mean, that's the reason I'm here.

329
00:23:12,383 --> 00:23:14,982
That's why I wanna
win, I wanna win for them.

330
00:23:15,023 --> 00:23:17,862
What about you, George?
Why are you still up there?

331
00:23:17,903 --> 00:23:19,702
I'm here for my family as well.

332
00:23:21,663 --> 00:23:24,662
I've proved what I needed
to prove here already -

333
00:23:24,703 --> 00:23:28,422
that I'm a great operator -
but I'm now here for them.

334
00:23:28,463 --> 00:23:30,742
We're here for you.

335
00:23:30,783 --> 00:23:33,662
- I would have given up by now.
- No, no, don't give up.

336
00:23:33,703 --> 00:23:35,142
Keep going.

337
00:23:36,783 --> 00:23:39,102
Hayley, why are you up there?

338
00:23:39,143 --> 00:23:41,062
I just wanna prove
to myself I can do it.

339
00:23:43,183 --> 00:23:45,302
I feel like I can, I feel
like my body can do it

340
00:23:45,343 --> 00:23:49,862
and my mind can do it,
and I just wanna hold on.

341
00:24:01,703 --> 00:24:03,422
I think we should
turn it up a little bit.

342
00:24:06,583 --> 00:24:08,342
Or in this case, turn it down.

343
00:24:10,223 --> 00:24:13,342
We're gonna bring it down again.

344
00:24:15,303 --> 00:24:16,382
Three...

345
00:24:18,183 --> 00:24:19,183
..two...

346
00:24:21,183 --> 00:24:22,222
..one.

347
00:24:32,583 --> 00:24:34,342
Those quads.

348
00:24:38,543 --> 00:24:40,822
Not too many comfortable positions now.

349
00:24:42,943 --> 00:24:47,742
Fewer and fewer options
the lower that ceiling gets.

350
00:24:51,983 --> 00:24:53,742
It's just like you're on a surfboard.

351
00:24:53,783 --> 00:24:55,822
Yeah.

352
00:25:15,103 --> 00:25:16,742
God, look at the sky behind us.

353
00:25:18,303 --> 00:25:19,502
Whoa.

354
00:25:20,623 --> 00:25:22,102
Oh, that looks so good.

355
00:25:23,223 --> 00:25:26,662
That will be someone's
last sunset, tonight.

356
00:25:40,383 --> 00:25:44,782
Guys, you've been
up there for 3.5 hours.

357
00:25:57,663 --> 00:25:59,582
Everyone checking each other out.

358
00:26:01,823 --> 00:26:08,302
Wondering who has the
most in the tank on day 47.

359
00:26:14,183 --> 00:26:19,062
We're now at the point where it
switches from a physical challenge

360
00:26:19,103 --> 00:26:22,182
to a mental challenge.

361
00:26:22,223 --> 00:26:27,022
Those pegs have gotta feel
like daggers in your feet now,

362
00:26:27,063 --> 00:26:29,222
boring through the flesh.

363
00:26:31,263 --> 00:26:33,662
Nothing easy about Survivor.

364
00:26:42,463 --> 00:26:45,502
George clearly in a lot of pain now.

365
00:26:45,543 --> 00:26:48,102
Come on, George.

366
00:26:48,143 --> 00:26:49,342
Moving around...

367
00:26:50,463 --> 00:26:52,062
..a lot now.

368
00:26:52,103 --> 00:26:53,622
Trying different positions.

369
00:26:55,743 --> 00:26:59,662
Looking for anything
that will offer some relief.

370
00:27:01,663 --> 00:27:04,702
We believe in you,
George. Keep fighting.

371
00:27:04,743 --> 00:27:06,862
You've got this, George, come on.

372
00:27:08,423 --> 00:27:09,822
I'm right here.

373
00:27:22,943 --> 00:27:24,342
Everyone still in it.

374
00:27:26,103 --> 00:27:30,302
Everyone still with a
shot at that necklace.

375
00:27:32,463 --> 00:27:34,382
George continues to fight.

376
00:27:35,863 --> 00:27:39,062
Stepped away from a
couple of other challenges.

377
00:27:40,903 --> 00:27:42,302
Not this time.

378
00:27:44,783 --> 00:27:47,342
How long can he keep this going for?

379
00:27:57,183 --> 00:27:58,982
I think I've gotta do it.

380
00:28:06,463 --> 00:28:07,862
I can't do any more.

381
00:28:07,903 --> 00:28:09,502
- Well done, George.
- Good job, George.

382
00:28:09,543 --> 00:28:15,382
And after over 4.5 hours,
George has had enough.

383
00:28:15,423 --> 00:28:17,102
He's out of the challenge.

384
00:28:17,143 --> 00:28:19,542
- Yeah, great effort, George.
- That's amazing.

385
00:28:19,583 --> 00:28:21,622
I'm so proud of you.

386
00:28:21,663 --> 00:28:24,142
- My hands couldn't hold on anymore.
- That's fine, son.

387
00:28:24,183 --> 00:28:26,702
- You did so good.
- That's fine.

388
00:28:26,743 --> 00:28:30,022
It's now down to Hayley and Flick.

389
00:28:32,863 --> 00:28:34,662
We now have a showdown.

390
00:28:35,783 --> 00:28:37,782
Fighting it out for that necklace.

391
00:28:39,103 --> 00:28:41,742
A guaranteed spot final two.

392
00:28:52,303 --> 00:28:57,702
Incredible effort from
both Hayley and Flick.

393
00:28:57,743 --> 00:29:04,062
Now it's time to drop
those spikes one last time.

394
00:29:04,103 --> 00:29:05,782
Hold on, Hayley. You got this.

395
00:29:07,743 --> 00:29:09,222
I'm gonna count you guys in.

396
00:29:13,263 --> 00:29:14,263
Three...

397
00:29:15,463 --> 00:29:18,342
..two... one.

398
00:29:27,743 --> 00:29:29,422
Oh, shit.

399
00:29:37,143 --> 00:29:39,502
It's now exactly one metre...

400
00:29:40,863 --> 00:29:45,062
..between the peg and
the spike above your head.

401
00:29:48,343 --> 00:29:50,422
Very little room to move around now.

402
00:29:55,023 --> 00:29:56,662
If it was painful before...

403
00:29:58,703 --> 00:30:00,982
..this is gonna become
a whole new level.

404
00:30:07,583 --> 00:30:09,702
Keep going, Hayley. Keep going.

405
00:30:12,463 --> 00:30:14,862
Flick, really struggling.

406
00:30:17,263 --> 00:30:18,662
Gasping for air.

407
00:30:21,743 --> 00:30:24,262
Pain is just unbearable.

408
00:30:26,183 --> 00:30:30,662
Meanwhile, Hayley is like a statue.

409
00:30:30,703 --> 00:30:33,342
Eyes closed, super focused.

410
00:30:34,903 --> 00:30:38,222
An expert on pain management.

411
00:30:38,263 --> 00:30:40,702
If Hayley is in pain,

412
00:30:40,743 --> 00:30:42,982
she's not showing it.

413
00:30:43,023 --> 00:30:45,382
Maybe that's part of her strategy.

414
00:30:48,023 --> 00:30:50,222
I don't know if I can
go much longer, hey?

415
00:30:50,263 --> 00:30:52,462
Yes, you can.
Come on. A little bit longer.

416
00:30:52,503 --> 00:30:53,662
Come on, Flick.

417
00:30:53,703 --> 00:30:56,702
Flick in excruciating pain,

418
00:30:56,743 --> 00:30:59,022
really trying to push.

419
00:31:03,343 --> 00:31:05,342
Flick's arms failing her now.

420
00:31:08,863 --> 00:31:11,342
Doing everything she can to hang on.

421
00:31:14,383 --> 00:31:17,502
Getting dangerously close
to the end of those spikes.

422
00:31:21,143 --> 00:31:22,822
Come on. dig deep.

423
00:31:22,863 --> 00:31:24,662
Find that strength, Flick.

424
00:31:24,703 --> 00:31:26,542
That last little bit.

425
00:31:52,623 --> 00:31:55,302
Come on, we're all here. You're OK.

426
00:31:55,343 --> 00:31:56,622
You're OK.

427
00:31:56,663 --> 00:31:58,022
Oh...

428
00:32:06,823 --> 00:32:09,222
You've got this. Keep
breathing through it.

429
00:32:22,023 --> 00:32:24,022
Stay there, Flick. Stay in the zone.

430
00:32:26,463 --> 00:32:27,742
That's good.

431
00:32:30,823 --> 00:32:33,422
Amazingly, Flick is still in it.

432
00:32:38,063 --> 00:32:40,622
Finding something in a reserve tank.

433
00:32:44,103 --> 00:32:46,662
That's it. Keep it up.

434
00:32:48,663 --> 00:32:50,782
You're strong. You can do this.

435
00:33:06,663 --> 00:33:08,742
Hayley's body shaking now.

436
00:33:18,863 --> 00:33:21,142
Who's going to reach their limit first?

437
00:33:21,183 --> 00:33:24,382
Keep going, Hayley.
Keep going. So strong.

438
00:33:24,423 --> 00:33:27,702
Yeah. Come on, Flick. Come on!

439
00:33:27,743 --> 00:33:30,222
Literally nowhere to go.

440
00:33:31,903 --> 00:33:33,222
Nowhere to hide.

441
00:33:34,943 --> 00:33:37,542
It's just you and the pain.

442
00:33:55,383 --> 00:33:57,902
I need help. I need help. I need help.

443
00:33:59,263 --> 00:34:00,742
- Getting off.
- Getting off?

444
00:34:00,783 --> 00:34:02,542
- Yeah. I need help.
- Alright.

445
00:34:02,583 --> 00:34:04,822
Well done.

446
00:34:04,863 --> 00:34:06,662
Are you right?

447
00:34:08,063 --> 00:34:11,542
After five hours and 17 minutes,

448
00:34:11,583 --> 00:34:13,982
Flick can no longer endure the pain.

449
00:34:14,023 --> 00:34:16,262
Well done, Hayley.

450
00:34:17,663 --> 00:34:20,382
Hayley wins immunity.

451
00:34:20,423 --> 00:34:23,342
And guarantees herself a spot,

452
00:34:23,383 --> 00:34:25,102
in the final tribal council.

453
00:34:25,143 --> 00:34:26,462
That was amazing.

454
00:34:26,503 --> 00:34:28,062
It really was amazing.

455
00:34:28,103 --> 00:34:31,142
- Oh, my God. Oh.
- Good job.

456
00:34:35,903 --> 00:34:37,982
Hayley, come on over.

457
00:34:38,023 --> 00:34:40,382
Well done.

458
00:34:42,223 --> 00:34:43,702
Congratulations.

459
00:34:43,743 --> 00:34:47,262
Individual immunity is yours.

460
00:34:47,303 --> 00:34:51,182
Guaranteed a 50%
shot at winning the game

461
00:34:51,223 --> 00:34:54,142
and the half million
dollars that goes with it.

462
00:34:55,583 --> 00:34:57,582
One big decision left,

463
00:34:57,623 --> 00:35:00,542
which of these two is going
to join you at that fund tribal?

464
00:35:00,583 --> 00:35:04,862
And which is going to become the
ninth and final member of the jury?

465
00:35:04,903 --> 00:35:06,822
Unfortunately, you won't
have much time to think about it

466
00:35:06,863 --> 00:35:08,622
because we're going
to go straight to tribal.

467
00:35:08,663 --> 00:35:10,542
We'll see you soon. Well done.

468
00:35:10,583 --> 00:35:13,742
Good job, Hayley. Amazing. Amazing.

469
00:35:16,623 --> 00:35:18,902
Oh, thank you so much for coming.

470
00:35:18,943 --> 00:35:20,582
Whatever happens happens. OK?

471
00:35:20,623 --> 00:35:22,942
I want you to be happy
that you got this far.

472
00:35:22,983 --> 00:35:24,702
- OK?
- Yeah. I am happy.

473
00:35:24,743 --> 00:35:26,422
You're OK.

474
00:35:27,823 --> 00:35:32,102
Losing that challenge
was really devastating for me.

475
00:35:32,143 --> 00:35:36,182
But my time is not up yet in the game.

476
00:35:36,223 --> 00:35:39,622
And I still have one more
chance to convince Hayley

477
00:35:39,663 --> 00:35:41,502
to take me to final tonight.

478
00:35:41,543 --> 00:35:43,062
- Bye.
- See you, guys.

479
00:35:43,103 --> 00:35:45,142
- See you. Love you.
- Bye, George.

480
00:35:45,183 --> 00:35:47,502
And I'm not going to
go down without a fight.

481
00:36:17,483 --> 00:36:19,922
I'll now bring in the
members of our jury.

482
00:36:19,963 --> 00:36:22,002
Baden,

483
00:36:22,043 --> 00:36:23,362
Gerald,

484
00:36:23,403 --> 00:36:25,202
Laura, Emmett,

485
00:36:25,243 --> 00:36:27,762
Andrew, Dani,

486
00:36:27,803 --> 00:36:29,642
Wai

487
00:36:29,683 --> 00:36:33,802
and Cara, voted out
at the last tribal council.

488
00:36:37,363 --> 00:36:39,162
Well done, Hayley.

489
00:36:41,963 --> 00:36:45,562
Well done today, guys. I mean,
that was a brutal challenge.

490
00:36:45,603 --> 00:36:48,842
And you guys gave it everything.

491
00:36:48,883 --> 00:36:51,122
But after five hours and 17 minutes,

492
00:36:51,163 --> 00:36:54,482
it was Hayley who
took that necklace again.

493
00:36:54,523 --> 00:36:58,042
Hayley, you seemed confident
from the get-go in that challenge.

494
00:36:58,083 --> 00:37:01,642
Did your confidence ever waver?

495
00:37:01,683 --> 00:37:05,282
Oh, I knew that it was
going to be gruelling

496
00:37:05,323 --> 00:37:08,642
because these two guys
really wanted it as well.

497
00:37:08,683 --> 00:37:14,042
And I took everything that I
have ever learned about pain

498
00:37:14,083 --> 00:37:15,762
and I used that today

499
00:37:15,803 --> 00:37:20,002
to make sure that I was the
last one wearing this necklace.

500
00:37:20,043 --> 00:37:22,682
So, I'm certainly
very proud of this win.

501
00:37:22,723 --> 00:37:26,922
Honestly, it was an amazing
performance, like, incredible.

502
00:37:28,443 --> 00:37:30,362
Well, Flick and George,

503
00:37:30,403 --> 00:37:33,482
you should both be very
proud of your efforts today,

504
00:37:33,523 --> 00:37:37,042
but, Hayley, you now have
the difficult decision to make -

505
00:37:37,083 --> 00:37:39,762
who are you going to send to the jury

506
00:37:39,803 --> 00:37:43,002
and who are you going to take
with you to the final tribal council?

507
00:37:43,043 --> 00:37:46,642
What's going through
your head right now?

508
00:37:46,683 --> 00:37:48,722
There's a lot of things
going through my head.

509
00:37:48,763 --> 00:37:50,842
I think ultimately this decision

510
00:37:50,883 --> 00:37:55,682
has to come down to who
do you think you can sit next to

511
00:37:55,723 --> 00:37:59,762
and convince the jury that you
have played a better game than them.

512
00:37:59,803 --> 00:38:02,562
But both of these guys
have played great games.

513
00:38:02,603 --> 00:38:05,242
Yeah. And so it's a
tough decision for me.

514
00:38:08,243 --> 00:38:09,762
Flick, let me ask you this,

515
00:38:09,803 --> 00:38:13,322
why should Hayley
take you to the final two?

516
00:38:13,363 --> 00:38:16,642
I don't know if I've ever seen
anyone play like George before.

517
00:38:16,683 --> 00:38:20,962
I look at George and
his game is amazing.

518
00:38:21,003 --> 00:38:24,642
And I would be worried about
coming up against someone

519
00:38:24,683 --> 00:38:26,602
who is so wise with their words.

520
00:38:26,643 --> 00:38:29,442
And I feel like that
is what has the power

521
00:38:29,483 --> 00:38:31,602
to sway the jury in the end.

522
00:38:35,723 --> 00:38:40,042
So, George, Flick has
laid out all the reasons

523
00:38:40,083 --> 00:38:42,362
why Hayley shouldn't take you.

524
00:38:42,403 --> 00:38:44,802
Why shouldn't Hayley take Flick?

525
00:38:48,403 --> 00:38:51,002
Because if Hayley wants to win $500,000,

526
00:38:51,043 --> 00:38:53,042
she should try and beat me.

527
00:38:55,323 --> 00:39:00,322
Are you saying that Flick has a
better chance of winning than Hayley?

528
00:39:00,363 --> 00:39:06,962
I think that Flick has more
locked in votes with that jury.

529
00:39:07,003 --> 00:39:11,562
And based on that, you have
to navigate a very thin line

530
00:39:11,603 --> 00:39:13,082
to get to the crown.

531
00:39:13,123 --> 00:39:17,762
My understanding is that there
are votes up for grab on that jury,

532
00:39:17,803 --> 00:39:19,962
but not all of them.

533
00:39:20,003 --> 00:39:23,882
And you have to factor that
into your decision tonight.

534
00:39:25,923 --> 00:39:28,962
I disagree. I don't think
I have locked in votes.

535
00:39:29,003 --> 00:39:31,202
I don't think anyone
has locked in votes.

536
00:39:31,243 --> 00:39:34,722
I mean, yeah, everyone
here is closer to certain people

537
00:39:34,763 --> 00:39:37,322
that are sitting over
there on that jury.

538
00:39:37,363 --> 00:39:40,322
But we can't expect that just
because we're close to these people

539
00:39:40,363 --> 00:39:42,482
that they're going to
vote for us in the end.

540
00:39:46,003 --> 00:39:47,722
Alright. Well, Hayley,

541
00:39:47,763 --> 00:39:51,122
tonight, your vote is
the only one that counts.

542
00:39:51,163 --> 00:39:53,682
And before we go and do that,

543
00:39:53,723 --> 00:39:57,242
George, what do you
want to say to Hayley?

544
00:39:57,283 --> 00:39:58,562
Queen Haley?

545
00:39:58,603 --> 00:40:00,842
What is a queen without a king?

546
00:40:00,883 --> 00:40:03,402
Save me from the guillotine tonight

547
00:40:03,443 --> 00:40:06,042
and take me to your final two tomorrow

548
00:40:06,083 --> 00:40:09,882
and let the king and queen
battle it out for the crown.

549
00:40:12,203 --> 00:40:14,602
Flick, is there anything
that you wanted to say?

550
00:40:16,123 --> 00:40:18,322
Oh, well...

551
00:40:19,403 --> 00:40:23,842
..for me to get to the end would
be a massive achievement...

552
00:40:25,243 --> 00:40:29,202
..with everything that I've
experienced on this crazy journey.

553
00:40:29,243 --> 00:40:31,802
Just to know that I never gave up,

554
00:40:31,843 --> 00:40:35,002
no matter what
challenge I was faced with.

555
00:40:35,043 --> 00:40:39,922
It would just reinforce why I'm here

556
00:40:39,963 --> 00:40:43,722
and give me the satisfaction
that I made it to the end.

557
00:40:43,763 --> 00:40:46,762
But tonight, the power
lies in Hayley's hands

558
00:40:46,803 --> 00:40:50,482
and Hayley will do what
is best for Hayley tonight.

559
00:40:50,523 --> 00:40:53,042
And I hope that's me.

560
00:40:57,283 --> 00:40:59,122
Well, Flick and George,

561
00:40:59,163 --> 00:41:02,202
you should both be very
proud of your efforts today,

562
00:41:02,243 --> 00:41:06,202
but Hayley, you now have
the difficult decision to make -

563
00:41:06,243 --> 00:41:08,602
who are you going to send to the jury

564
00:41:08,643 --> 00:41:12,082
and who are you going to take
with you to the final tribal council?

565
00:41:14,083 --> 00:41:16,442
It's time for you to cast that vote.

566
00:41:16,483 --> 00:41:17,483
Oh, man...

567
00:42:07,603 --> 00:42:08,842
I'll go collect the vote.

568
00:42:38,483 --> 00:42:39,922
I'll read the vote.

569
00:42:47,283 --> 00:42:49,882
22nd person voted out

570
00:42:49,923 --> 00:42:52,882
and ninth and final
member of our jury...

571
00:42:55,243 --> 00:42:57,322
..Flick.

572
00:43:00,003 --> 00:43:01,482
You need to bring me your torch.

573
00:43:04,603 --> 00:43:06,082
- I'm sorry.
- No. It's all good.

574
00:43:06,123 --> 00:43:07,123
It's all good.

575
00:43:10,563 --> 00:43:12,722
Congrats.

576
00:43:14,443 --> 00:43:15,882
- Thanks, George.
- You really did.

577
00:43:15,923 --> 00:43:18,042
Thanks, George.

578
00:43:18,083 --> 00:43:19,362
Proud of you guys.

579
00:43:19,403 --> 00:43:22,402
I'm just so grateful and thankful

580
00:43:22,443 --> 00:43:25,482
to have made it to the
top three with you guys.

581
00:43:27,043 --> 00:43:28,722
Thank you.

582
00:43:31,323 --> 00:43:34,562
- Flick, the tribe has spoken.
- Yes, they have.

583
00:43:37,523 --> 00:43:38,682
Time for you to go.

584
00:43:42,963 --> 00:43:43,963
Wow.

585
00:43:51,163 --> 00:43:56,242
Well, congratulations,
you are the final two.

586
00:43:56,283 --> 00:43:58,962
You've gone as far as
you can go in this game

587
00:43:59,003 --> 00:44:03,562
and now the power shifts
to these guys, the jury.

588
00:44:03,603 --> 00:44:06,442
So, I suggest you get some rest

589
00:44:06,483 --> 00:44:08,242
and think about how are
you going to convince them

590
00:44:08,283 --> 00:44:10,802
that you deserve the
title of Sole Survivor

591
00:44:10,843 --> 00:44:13,122
and the half million that goes with it.

592
00:44:13,163 --> 00:44:15,482
- Grab your torches and head on out.
- Oh, yeah. I need that.

593
00:44:15,523 --> 00:44:17,722
Congrats.

594
00:44:17,763 --> 00:44:19,122
- See ya.
- Bye.

595
00:44:19,163 --> 00:44:21,962
Goodbye. See you.

596
00:44:55,377 --> 00:44:56,860
Yum!

597
00:44:56,860 --> 00:44:58,300
Oh, finally!

598
00:44:58,300 --> 00:45:00,900
- Oh, my God.
- Oh!

599
00:45:01,017 --> 00:45:02,180
Bacon.

600
00:45:02,180 --> 00:45:05,140
- Oh, my God. More bacon. Eggs.
- Eggs.

601
00:45:05,140 --> 00:45:07,023
Oh, my God. Oh, yum.

602
00:45:07,163 --> 00:45:10,802
Last night, I won the
final immunity challenge.

603
00:45:10,843 --> 00:45:13,162
I had the necklace and I got
to choose who went home.

604
00:45:13,203 --> 00:45:15,882
And I sent Flick home.

605
00:45:17,003 --> 00:45:20,282
To send her home was
the most difficult thing

606
00:45:20,323 --> 00:45:21,562
I've had to do in this game.

607
00:45:23,123 --> 00:45:25,602
I grew really close
to Flick in this game,

608
00:45:25,643 --> 00:45:27,922
but it was the only
thing I could think to do

609
00:45:27,963 --> 00:45:29,882
to give myself a chance to win.

610
00:45:29,923 --> 00:45:33,682
This is the moment
I've been waiting for.

611
00:45:33,723 --> 00:45:35,842
- Ooh!
- Yay!

612
00:45:35,883 --> 00:45:37,482
- Top two.
- Let it pour.

613
00:45:37,523 --> 00:45:42,442
I think that my game
stacks up against George's.

614
00:45:42,483 --> 00:45:46,282
His strategy has been incredible,
but what he missed out on

615
00:45:46,323 --> 00:45:48,322
is playing a physical game,

616
00:45:48,363 --> 00:45:51,202
and he's kind of rubbed
some people the wrong way.

617
00:45:51,243 --> 00:45:54,842
To 48 days of fun,
and good luck tonight.

618
00:45:54,883 --> 00:45:57,802
- Yeah, may the best man win.
- Cheers.

619
00:45:57,843 --> 00:46:02,442
I have a winning game because it
encompasses all aspects of Survivor.

620
00:46:02,483 --> 00:46:05,282
- Let's cook.
- Let's get started with the food.

621
00:46:05,323 --> 00:46:07,442
I've been incredibly physical.

622
00:46:07,483 --> 00:46:11,402
I took out four individual
immunity necklaces.

623
00:46:11,443 --> 00:46:15,442
I've played very smart, strategic
moves and taken out big players.

624
00:46:16,683 --> 00:46:19,282
And I've made great social bonds.

625
00:46:20,443 --> 00:46:24,802
Now I'm at the end because I
have come up against 22 people

626
00:46:24,843 --> 00:46:27,322
and I outmanoeuvred them.

627
00:46:27,363 --> 00:46:29,482
Last day in Survivor.

628
00:46:29,523 --> 00:46:32,242
I know. This is gonna be a fun day.

629
00:46:32,283 --> 00:46:36,522
I've spent a lot of the
last decade studying

630
00:46:36,563 --> 00:46:39,402
because I wanted to have
a career that helped people.

631
00:46:40,763 --> 00:46:43,522
But it means that I've
had to sacrifice so much.

632
00:46:44,683 --> 00:46:48,242
Half a million dollars would
completely change my life.

633
00:46:48,283 --> 00:46:51,562
I can buy a house, buy a car.

634
00:46:51,603 --> 00:46:53,402
It would be incredible.

635
00:46:53,443 --> 00:46:55,402
To start a family.

636
00:46:55,443 --> 00:46:57,442
That would mean the world to me.

637
00:46:57,483 --> 00:47:00,762
I didn't win many rewards off
Fire tribe, but do you know what?

638
00:47:00,803 --> 00:47:03,522
I'm happy to get to day
48, top two breakfast.

639
00:47:04,803 --> 00:47:08,722
Never in a million years would
I have thought on day one,

640
00:47:08,763 --> 00:47:14,482
when I stood on that mat in my
white Bankstown Sports Club outfit,

641
00:47:14,523 --> 00:47:18,242
that I would be getting ready
to make a pitch to the jury

642
00:47:18,283 --> 00:47:20,562
at tonight's tribal council.

643
00:47:20,603 --> 00:47:24,242
Well, if my mum was proud of me
for doing that final immunity challenge,

644
00:47:24,283 --> 00:47:27,082
wait until she sees
me stirring tomatoes.

645
00:47:27,123 --> 00:47:28,762
Whoo!

646
00:47:28,803 --> 00:47:32,402
Yesterday's immunity challenge
reminded me why I'm here.

647
00:47:32,443 --> 00:47:35,362
It's my family. I came here for them.

648
00:47:36,483 --> 00:47:38,842
My hardworking father and mother,

649
00:47:38,883 --> 00:47:43,362
they've been working for over 40
years, and they've worked enough.

650
00:47:43,403 --> 00:47:47,082
I came here to win half a million
dollars that clears their debt

651
00:47:47,123 --> 00:47:49,922
and allows them to
finally enjoy their life.

652
00:47:52,203 --> 00:47:57,042
My family have been there for
me and I wanna be there for them.

653
00:47:57,083 --> 00:47:59,802
I'm gonna make sure
that I can deliver for them.

654
00:47:59,843 --> 00:48:02,082
Breakfast of the king and the queen.

655
00:48:02,123 --> 00:48:04,482
We need this breakfast 'cause
we've got a battle ahead of us today.

656
00:48:04,523 --> 00:48:07,082
- Mm-hm.
- It is gonna be a huge tribal.

657
00:48:09,603 --> 00:48:13,522
I've had a target on my back
for almost every single day

658
00:48:13,563 --> 00:48:15,202
here in the game.

659
00:48:15,243 --> 00:48:17,042
People have been firing shots at me

660
00:48:17,083 --> 00:48:19,682
but they haven't been able to hit me,

661
00:48:19,723 --> 00:48:24,242
and that hasn't been through luck,
it's been through sheer hard work.

662
00:48:24,283 --> 00:48:29,562
I knew I had to outwit and
outplay people to outlast them,

663
00:48:29,603 --> 00:48:32,122
and that's what I did.

664
00:48:32,163 --> 00:48:35,882
Almost every single
person is sitting on that jury

665
00:48:35,923 --> 00:48:39,482
because I orchestrated
their elimination.

666
00:48:39,523 --> 00:48:42,922
I'm hoping that that jury
doesn't have grievances.

667
00:48:42,963 --> 00:48:45,922
What I need to do with
the jury tonight is show them

668
00:48:45,963 --> 00:48:49,282
that you don't need to
like me to vote for me,

669
00:48:49,323 --> 00:48:51,242
you just need to acknowledge

670
00:48:51,283 --> 00:48:55,362
that what I've done
is worthy of the title.

671
00:48:57,083 --> 00:48:59,042
- That's it for the Fire tribe.
- That's it.

672
00:48:59,083 --> 00:49:03,602
King George against Queen
Hayley truly is a battle royale.

673
00:49:04,723 --> 00:49:09,602
And I'm going to snatch the
crown that I so rightfully deserve.

674
00:49:42,421 --> 00:49:44,580
Then there were two.

675
00:49:46,220 --> 00:49:48,019
I'll now bring in the
members of our jury.

676
00:49:50,660 --> 00:49:53,939
Baden, Gerald,

677
00:49:53,980 --> 00:49:55,779
Laura,

678
00:49:55,820 --> 00:49:58,939
Emmett, Andrew...

679
00:50:00,660 --> 00:50:03,939
..Dani, Wai...

680
00:50:05,780 --> 00:50:08,379
..Cara and Flick...

681
00:50:09,420 --> 00:50:11,459
..voted out at the last tribal council.

682
00:50:17,500 --> 00:50:19,379
- So, here we are...
- Yeah.

683
00:50:19,420 --> 00:50:23,339
..day 48 and your final tribal council.

684
00:50:23,380 --> 00:50:27,779
You guys have gone as far as
you can possibly go in this game.

685
00:50:27,820 --> 00:50:31,179
Tonight the power
now shifts to the jury.

686
00:50:32,580 --> 00:50:35,419
Nine people that you had a
hand in voting out either directly

687
00:50:35,460 --> 00:50:38,419
or indirectly will now
decide which of you two

688
00:50:38,460 --> 00:50:40,259
deserves the title of Sole Survivor

689
00:50:40,300 --> 00:50:42,179
and the half a million
dollars that goes with it.

690
00:50:43,500 --> 00:50:47,099
This is how it's gonna work. You'll
each make an opening statement.

691
00:50:47,140 --> 00:50:49,539
This is your chance to pitch to the jury

692
00:50:49,580 --> 00:50:52,739
why you think you
deserve to win this game.

693
00:50:52,780 --> 00:50:55,539
Then the jury will address
you, they'll ask you questions

694
00:50:55,580 --> 00:50:57,259
and you'll answer them.

695
00:50:57,300 --> 00:50:59,979
And then they'll have a chance
to respond to your answers

696
00:51:00,020 --> 00:51:01,539
in an open forum.

697
00:51:01,580 --> 00:51:03,259
Once everyone's had their say,

698
00:51:03,300 --> 00:51:05,579
the jury will then go up to vote

699
00:51:05,620 --> 00:51:09,979
to decide who wins Australian
Survivor: Brains v Brawn.

700
00:51:11,140 --> 00:51:13,899
George, this is the moment
you've been waiting for.

701
00:51:13,940 --> 00:51:16,659
You now get to address the jury.

702
00:51:20,860 --> 00:51:23,859
Well, good evening, jury.

703
00:51:23,900 --> 00:51:29,379
To my friends and my frenemies,
what a journey we've all been on.

704
00:51:29,420 --> 00:51:32,979
I came here as a political operative.

705
00:51:33,020 --> 00:51:34,739
I've never been camping before.

706
00:51:34,780 --> 00:51:39,459
When I stepped on that mat in
day one and saw the lot of you,

707
00:51:39,500 --> 00:51:42,659
I told myself, "What the hell
have I gotten myself into?"

708
00:51:42,700 --> 00:51:48,499
But I've been overcoming
personal barriers since the very start.

709
00:51:48,540 --> 00:51:52,619
And it worked like this, phase
one was controlled dysfunction,

710
00:51:52,660 --> 00:51:54,619
it was controlled chaos.

711
00:51:54,660 --> 00:51:58,459
I realised I was in a
minority from the outset.

712
00:51:58,500 --> 00:52:03,419
That tribe had a dynamic that was
gonna pick off the physically weak.

713
00:52:03,460 --> 00:52:06,819
That's why I had to
change the tone of the game

714
00:52:06,860 --> 00:52:09,819
at the very first Brains tribal council.

715
00:52:09,860 --> 00:52:13,339
Because if it relied
on an interpretation

716
00:52:13,380 --> 00:52:17,419
of physical strength
as being the key criteria,

717
00:52:17,460 --> 00:52:21,459
I would be right at the
bottom of the pecking order.

718
00:52:21,500 --> 00:52:26,419
I made a decision to save
who I thought needed saving.

719
00:52:26,460 --> 00:52:31,419
Giving Wai a second chance
made sure that I got here.

720
00:52:33,860 --> 00:52:40,259
My game moved to a second phase
at tribe swap. It was maintenance.

721
00:52:40,300 --> 00:52:45,659
And at the maintenance phase,
I had to rely on my social game.

722
00:52:45,700 --> 00:52:48,499
I became an honorary Brawn

723
00:52:48,540 --> 00:52:51,979
and that set me up for
the final phase of my game.

724
00:52:53,580 --> 00:52:55,699
Dynasty.

725
00:52:55,740 --> 00:53:01,459
When we got to the merge I
realised my best prospect of success

726
00:53:01,500 --> 00:53:03,659
was going back to the Brains.

727
00:53:03,700 --> 00:53:07,619
Because the Brawn
alliance had what I don't -

728
00:53:07,660 --> 00:53:10,459
its physical prowess.

729
00:53:10,500 --> 00:53:13,699
So I had to cook up
a very, very risky plan.

730
00:53:14,980 --> 00:53:19,019
I was playing two
alliances as a covert agent.

731
00:53:19,060 --> 00:53:23,459
I risked my entire future in the
game, when I was in a comfortable,

732
00:53:23,500 --> 00:53:29,859
safe Brawn majority, to help all the
Brains, because I was Brain strong.

733
00:53:29,900 --> 00:53:35,739
And in working with the Brains
I carried a minority to a majority.
