Gerry had enough, drops out.

360
00:20:37,200 --> 00:20:38,760
We're down to three,

361
00:20:38,760 --> 00:20:41,840
Matt, Liz and George,

362
00:20:41,840 --> 00:20:45,720
battling it out for one necklace.

363
00:20:45,720 --> 00:20:48,040
One guarantee

364
00:20:48,040 --> 00:20:51,240
of absolute safety tonight.

365
00:20:51,240 --> 00:20:53,840
(TENSE MUSIC)

366
00:21:17,040 --> 00:21:19,720
Alright. You've been at it
for two hours.

367
00:21:19,720 --> 00:21:22,520
Time for us to turn up the heat.

368
00:21:24,480 --> 00:21:25,560
Here we go.

369
00:21:30,360 --> 00:21:32,840
24cm of spike.

370
00:21:35,760 --> 00:21:37,320
(GRUNTS)

371
00:21:38,440 --> 00:21:40,240
Ooh!

372
00:21:40,240 --> 00:21:44,280
Those spikes really have you
stretched out now.

373
00:21:44,280 --> 00:21:48,760
Lot of pain with every readjustment.

374
00:21:50,200 --> 00:21:53,000
The further out they come, the
harder it's gonna be to readjust.

375
00:21:53,000 --> 00:21:55,200
Yeah. It's really hard already!

376
00:21:56,280 --> 00:22:00,080
The sun, the wind, the rain,

377
00:22:00,080 --> 00:22:03,120
the angry ocean smashing you.

378
00:22:05,680 --> 00:22:08,480
It's all gonna take its toll.

379
00:22:10,000 --> 00:22:12,760
So, George, it seems like
you have this one in the bag.

380
00:22:12,760 --> 00:22:13,920
I hope so.

381
00:22:13,920 --> 00:22:16,280
It'd be a good time
to win a challenge.

382
00:22:16,280 --> 00:22:19,040
Do you need to win it
or you just wanna win it?

383
00:22:20,480 --> 00:22:22,160
I think everyone needs to win it.

384
00:22:22,160 --> 00:22:24,560
It's the guaranteed way
to pitch to the jury.

385
00:22:24,560 --> 00:22:26,720
But I definitely want to win it.

386
00:22:26,720 --> 00:22:29,320
No-one wants this more than me,
I reckon.

387
00:22:31,480 --> 00:22:33,800
So, Liz, George thinks
he wants it more than you.

388
00:22:38,520 --> 00:22:40,800
George can think what he likes.

389
00:22:40,800 --> 00:22:42,480
(LAUGHS)

390
00:22:42,480 --> 00:22:45,520
We'll see who's the last one
standing, Georgie.

391
00:22:48,400 --> 00:22:49,880
We will see.

392
00:22:53,040 --> 00:22:55,000
(HAUNTING MELODY)

393
00:22:57,560 --> 00:23:00,440
(SUSPENSEFUL MUSIC)

394
00:23:07,600 --> 00:23:10,360
This challenge has been going
for three hours.

395
00:23:10,360 --> 00:23:13,200
Three hours. Well done, guys.
Well done, you guys.

396
00:23:13,200 --> 00:23:17,000
I think it's time to match
the aggression of the sea.

397
00:23:18,440 --> 00:23:20,720
Let's crank it again.

398
00:23:23,400 --> 00:23:25,440
This is where the rubber
meets the road.

399
00:23:35,040 --> 00:23:37,760
28cm of spike.

400
00:23:40,760 --> 00:23:42,240
(GRUNTS SOFTLY)

401
00:23:42,240 --> 00:23:44,880
George starting to shake now.

402
00:23:49,320 --> 00:23:51,600
Just cannot find any relief.

403
00:23:52,600 --> 00:23:53,960
Come on, Georgie.

404
00:23:55,120 --> 00:23:57,400
George really digging.

405
00:23:57,400 --> 00:23:59,360
Not giving up.

406
00:23:59,360 --> 00:24:02,080
Come on, George! You've got this!

407
00:24:02,080 --> 00:24:03,560
You've done double this.

408
00:24:07,440 --> 00:24:08,640
Argh!

409
00:24:08,640 --> 00:24:12,040
Big painful readjustment from George.

410
00:24:12,040 --> 00:24:13,320
Wow!

411
00:24:13,320 --> 00:24:16,760
I can feel that pain
all the way over here.

412
00:24:18,000 --> 00:24:21,160
Everything's gotta be hurting by now.

413
00:24:22,480 --> 00:24:24,440
GERRY: Unbelievable, guys!

414
00:24:24,440 --> 00:24:27,640
The whole three of you
deserve to win this challenge.

415
00:24:41,320 --> 00:24:44,440
George clearly in a lot of pain now.

416
00:24:45,760 --> 00:24:48,040
Find that next level, George!

417
00:24:57,720 --> 00:25:00,600
(GROANS) I think...I'm coming down.

418
00:25:01,640 --> 00:25:03,800
Ohhh.
(OTHERS APPLAUD)

419
00:25:03,800 --> 00:25:07,040
After three hours and 50 minutes,

420
00:25:07,040 --> 00:25:10,840
George cannot hang any longer.

421
00:25:10,840 --> 00:25:12,200
Amazing effort.

422
00:25:13,200 --> 00:25:14,720
Whoo-hoo!
Brilliant, Georgie.

423
00:25:20,200 --> 00:25:21,440
Oh!

424
00:25:21,440 --> 00:25:23,800
My legs are good.
It's just my arms are dead.

425
00:25:23,800 --> 00:25:26,000
Well done.
Thank you.

426
00:25:26,000 --> 00:25:27,960
PAM: Well done, George!
KIRSTIE: Well done!

427
00:25:27,960 --> 00:25:29,600
Now we have a showdown.

428
00:25:29,600 --> 00:25:31,640
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

429
00:25:32,640 --> 00:25:35,320
Hero versus villain.

430
00:25:35,320 --> 00:25:37,360
Matt taking on Liz.

431
00:25:37,360 --> 00:25:40,360
DANIEL: Come on, Liz!
KIRSTIE: You're doing so well, Matt!

432
00:25:40,360 --> 00:25:42,000
Doing so, so well.

433
00:25:42,000 --> 00:25:44,520
Who can stay up there the longest?

434
00:25:46,160 --> 00:25:48,680
Who's gonna take the honour

435
00:25:48,680 --> 00:25:50,520
of that final necklace?

436
00:26:18,720 --> 00:26:21,080
That is four hours.

437
00:26:23,160 --> 00:26:25,680
GERRY: Good on you, guys.
KIRSTIE: You can do this, Matt!

438
00:26:25,680 --> 00:26:26,760
Watch out!

439
00:26:26,760 --> 00:26:29,080
It's a mental game now.

440
00:26:30,240 --> 00:26:33,000
It's purely about
pushing through that pain.

441
00:26:34,160 --> 00:26:35,480
(EXHALES)

442
00:26:40,320 --> 00:26:42,560
CARA:

443
00:27:02,120 --> 00:27:05,480
Keep going! Keep going! Think of
everything you've been through.

444
00:27:05,480 --> 00:27:08,200
(MOMENTOUS MUSIC BUILDS)

445
00:27:11,360 --> 00:27:13,360
All the ups and downs.

446
00:27:14,720 --> 00:27:17,880
Keep pushing. Keep...
Just breathe and focus.

447
00:27:17,880 --> 00:27:19,720
You're almost there.

448
00:27:21,360 --> 00:27:23,360
You know how strong you are.

449
00:27:23,360 --> 00:27:25,760
Think of what this will mean to you
when you're home.

450
00:27:37,080 --> 00:27:38,920
You want to go again?

451
00:27:43,280 --> 00:27:45,600
Matt, Liz wants me to crank it again.

452
00:27:48,840 --> 00:27:50,400
Let's just do it.

453
00:27:51,440 --> 00:27:55,560
Alright, both Matt and Liz
want one more crank.

454
00:27:55,560 --> 00:27:57,160
Here it comes!

455
00:27:58,520 --> 00:28:01,080
(GEARS CREAK)

456
00:28:08,760 --> 00:28:10,720
That is it!

457
00:28:12,400 --> 00:28:15,960
That's a full 32cm of spike.

458
00:28:19,120 --> 00:28:21,120
Matt really shaking now.

459
00:28:28,400 --> 00:28:29,960
(WOOD CREAKS)

460
00:28:29,960 --> 00:28:31,600
Wow!

461
00:28:31,600 --> 00:28:33,400
Holy (BLEEP)!

462
00:28:33,400 --> 00:28:37,400
Trying to weave her way
to the other side.

463
00:28:45,360 --> 00:28:48,080
GEORGE:

464
00:28:54,480 --> 00:28:56,160
Ohh. Just...

465
00:28:59,080 --> 00:29:00,600
GEORGE:

466
00:29:06,560 --> 00:29:09,040
GEORGE:

467
00:29:18,000 --> 00:29:21,120
(INTENSE MUSIC)

468
00:29:21,120 --> 00:29:24,120
This is pure willpower now.

469
00:29:24,120 --> 00:29:26,640
DANIEL: Think of the pain
you've been through before.

470
00:29:26,640 --> 00:29:28,440
Think of what this means.

471
00:29:28,440 --> 00:29:31,640
Matt's struggling to hold on.

472
00:29:31,640 --> 00:29:35,440
Fingertips on the edge
of that handle.

473
00:29:40,360 --> 00:29:43,320
Fatigue and cold the obstacle now.

474
00:29:44,440 --> 00:29:47,040
Liz continues to shake.

475
00:29:47,040 --> 00:29:48,160
Keep breathing!

476
00:29:48,160 --> 00:29:50,200
Focus on your breathing!

477
00:29:51,760 --> 00:29:54,480
The pain is just unbearable.

478
00:30:05,640 --> 00:30:08,120
Oh!
Hand comes off.

479
00:30:09,960 --> 00:30:11,240
And that is it!

480
00:30:11,240 --> 00:30:13,760
GEORGE: Liz just won! You won, Liz!
CARA: Whoo!

481
00:30:13,760 --> 00:30:16,440
After four hours and 10 minutes,
Matt is out.

482
00:30:16,440 --> 00:30:17,440
Sit down!

483
00:30:17,440 --> 00:30:22,120
..and Liz wins final
individual immunity.

484
00:30:22,120 --> 00:30:23,560
(OTHERS APPLAUD)
Well done, you!

485
00:30:23,560 --> 00:30:26,600
Wow! What an effort.

486
00:30:29,120 --> 00:30:31,400
You did so, so well.

487
00:30:31,400 --> 00:30:32,880
You're amazing.

488
00:30:32,880 --> 00:30:34,280
Wow! (SOBS)

489
00:30:34,280 --> 00:30:36,520
You are a superwoman.

490
00:30:36,520 --> 00:30:38,280
(CHEERING AND APPLAUSE)

491
00:30:38,280 --> 00:30:39,600
CARA: Look at Georgie...

492
00:30:39,600 --> 00:30:41,440
You're amazing. (KISSES)

493
00:30:42,440 --> 00:30:45,800
(SOBS)

494
00:30:55,080 --> 00:30:57,320
Liz, come on over!
GEORGE: Well done, Liz!

495
00:30:57,320 --> 00:31:00,000
Well done.
Take your time, take your time.

496
00:31:00,000 --> 00:31:01,640
Oh, still jelly legs.

497
00:31:01,640 --> 00:31:03,200
(LAUGHS)

498
00:31:03,200 --> 00:31:04,680
Whoo!
Wow.

499
00:31:06,880 --> 00:31:09,880
Wow. What an effort.

500
00:31:10,880 --> 00:31:13,800
Individual immunity is yours.
GEORGE: Well done, Liz!

501
00:31:13,800 --> 00:31:18,800
Guaranteed a one-in-three shot
at winning the title

502
00:31:18,800 --> 00:31:21,200
and the half-million dollars
that goes with it.

503
00:31:21,200 --> 00:31:22,800
Daniel, how proud are you right now?

504
00:31:22,800 --> 00:31:26,000
Mate, she's a legend, eh?
GERRY: She is. She is indeed.

505
00:31:26,000 --> 00:31:27,880
Indeed. Well done.
That was a great effort.

506
00:31:27,880 --> 00:31:29,320
Thank you.
Alright.

507
00:31:29,320 --> 00:31:32,480
George, Matt, Gerry,
Tribal Council tonight,

508
00:31:32,480 --> 00:31:36,200
where one of you will become
the final member of our jury.

509
00:31:36,200 --> 00:31:39,360
It won't be you. Well done.
LIZ: Thank you!

510
00:31:39,360 --> 00:31:40,800
GEORGE: Well done again, Liz.

511
00:31:40,800 --> 00:31:43,520
Alright, I'll give you a minute
to say goodbye to your loved ones.

512
00:31:43,520 --> 00:31:45,200
Thank you, Cara.
Head back to camp.

513
00:31:45,200 --> 00:31:47,440
I'll see you in Double Bay
next week.

514
00:31:47,440 --> 00:31:49,760
And I'll see you tonight.
Thank you for coming.

515
00:31:49,760 --> 00:31:52,880
(LIZ SPEAKS INDISTINCTLY)
Oh, you made me happy seeing you.

516
00:31:52,880 --> 00:31:54,960
'Bye, guys!
Good luck.

517
00:31:54,960 --> 00:31:58,080
Nice to meet you, Kirstie.
See you, guys.

518
00:32:00,120 --> 00:32:03,560
The fact that Liz has won
is not good for me.

519
00:32:04,600 --> 00:32:06,960
Because she might
turn on me tonight.

520
00:32:08,200 --> 00:32:10,440
The stakes are really high.

521
00:32:10,440 --> 00:32:13,240
But strategy is the sport
that I'm good at.

522
00:32:14,240 --> 00:32:16,480
Liz might be the Olympian,

523
00:32:16,480 --> 00:32:18,840
but this is my Olympics

524
00:32:18,840 --> 00:32:20,920
and I'm here playing for gold.

525
00:32:27,000 --> 00:32:28,720
(SUSPENSEFUL MUSIC)

526
00:32:35,560 --> 00:32:36,720
(BIRDSONG)

527
00:32:46,160 --> 00:32:47,480
Thank you, George.

528
00:32:49,320 --> 00:32:51,280
Thank you.

529
00:32:51,280 --> 00:32:54,320
I'm in the top three
and it feels bloody good.

530
00:32:54,320 --> 00:32:56,760
It is such a special moment for me.

531
00:32:56,760 --> 00:32:58,440
Mmm.
Thank you.

532
00:32:58,440 --> 00:33:00,640
MATT: Absolute amazing effort.

533
00:33:00,640 --> 00:33:03,160
If I didn't win
this final challenge,

534
00:33:03,160 --> 00:33:07,520
Matt, Gerry and George
were sending me to the jury bench.

535
00:33:09,120 --> 00:33:11,440
Congratulations.

536
00:33:11,440 --> 00:33:13,720
Thank you, guys, thank you.
That was amazing. That was awesome.

537
00:33:13,720 --> 00:33:18,000
Now, the boys I can see...
they're petrified.

538
00:33:19,720 --> 00:33:23,000
Whereas I'm walking around
in my beautiful necklace.

539
00:33:24,360 --> 00:33:26,200
Do you reckon you could've lasted
way longer?

540
00:33:26,200 --> 00:33:27,720
Nah.
Ha!

541
00:33:27,720 --> 00:33:30,440
Tonight, my wicked, wicked plan

542
00:33:30,440 --> 00:33:33,120
is to send George
to that jury bench.

543
00:33:33,120 --> 00:33:37,920
George has blindsided me
three times in this game

544
00:33:37,920 --> 00:33:41,880
and this is my moment
to take revenge on George.

545
00:33:41,880 --> 00:33:43,280
(TENSE MUSIC)

546
00:33:43,280 --> 00:33:48,120
If I can pull it off,
this will be the perfect blindside.

547
00:33:49,520 --> 00:33:53,400
You...you wait till you see
the three of you.

548
00:33:53,400 --> 00:33:55,520
Just...it was incredible.
It was torturous.

549
00:33:55,520 --> 00:33:57,840
I am so humbled...to watch.
Thank you.

550
00:33:57,840 --> 00:33:59,680
Oh, thank you, Gerry.
That's so kind.

551
00:33:59,680 --> 00:34:01,640
So humbled to watch.
Thanks, Gerry.

552
00:34:03,240 --> 00:34:05,320
Such a good day.

553
00:34:05,320 --> 00:34:09,240
Met Kirstie, so...
Well, we don't have time for that.

554
00:34:09,240 --> 00:34:13,480
OK, well, let's...let's...let's have
a round table of conversation.

555
00:34:13,480 --> 00:34:15,920
Hmm.
Let's face it.

556
00:34:15,920 --> 00:34:19,040
Youse are all front-row contenders.

557
00:34:19,040 --> 00:34:20,280
OK?
Mm.

558
00:34:20,280 --> 00:34:24,760
I...am not worthy after
today's effort from you guys.

559
00:34:25,840 --> 00:34:28,040
No, listen to me. You guys...

560
00:34:28,040 --> 00:34:31,600
I'm just saying my thing
and I'll be open in front of Liz.

561
00:34:31,600 --> 00:34:32,600
Mm.
OK?

562
00:34:32,600 --> 00:34:35,120
'Cause I've always been as open
as I possibly can.

563
00:34:35,120 --> 00:34:38,880
At the end of the day,
I don't want to break any promises.

564
00:34:38,880 --> 00:34:40,960
You can go and have a talk
with yourselves.

565
00:34:42,600 --> 00:34:45,920
But I reckon put all votes on me.

566
00:34:48,040 --> 00:34:51,240
That's where I stand.
I'm happy to take...to cop the votes.

567
00:34:52,240 --> 00:34:54,720
I'll do my best tomorrow, Gerry.

568
00:34:54,720 --> 00:34:56,920
Yeah.
Thank you, Gerry.

569
00:34:56,920 --> 00:34:59,040
GEORGE: I can't believe it!

570
00:35:00,040 --> 00:35:03,320
I'm happy to send Gerry to the jury.
That's perfect.

571
00:35:03,320 --> 00:35:05,280
It's an extra vote.

572
00:35:05,280 --> 00:35:07,280
I think Gerry realises

573
00:35:07,280 --> 00:35:09,640
he might as well let
his best friend George win.

574
00:35:10,720 --> 00:35:15,960
Every single decision that
Gerry has made has benefited me.

575
00:35:15,960 --> 00:35:17,960
I mean that.
I will do it, Gerry.

576
00:35:17,960 --> 00:35:18,960
OK.

577
00:35:18,960 --> 00:35:22,760
And now my game comes down
to this one final move.

578
00:35:22,760 --> 00:35:25,040
I need to convince Matt and Liz

579
00:35:25,040 --> 00:35:28,920
that the best person to send
to the jury is Gerry.

580
00:35:28,920 --> 00:35:31,120
I have to pull this one off

581
00:35:31,120 --> 00:35:34,800
because it will determine
whether I win this game or not.

582
00:35:41,520 --> 00:35:44,360
(TENSE MUSIC)

583
00:35:44,360 --> 00:35:46,440
MATT:

584
00:35:46,440 --> 00:35:47,440
Um...

585
00:35:49,760 --> 00:35:51,840
Obviously I want to get to the end.
Yeah.

586
00:35:51,840 --> 00:35:54,680
And this gives us both a chance
to get to the end

587
00:35:54,680 --> 00:35:56,520
if we can vote for Gerry.

588
00:35:56,520 --> 00:35:58,360
I don't want to do it to him.
Yeah.

589
00:35:58,360 --> 00:36:00,240
I told him I'd never write
his name down.

590
00:36:00,240 --> 00:36:01,240
Yeah.

591
00:36:01,240 --> 00:36:04,240
But if the only way that
the two of us can get to the end

592
00:36:04,240 --> 00:36:07,360
is by voting Gerry,
it's our ticket to the end, Matt.

593
00:36:08,360 --> 00:36:10,640
We have to vote Gerry.
Yeah.

594
00:36:10,640 --> 00:36:12,400
We have to.

595
00:36:12,400 --> 00:36:14,880
It's sad, but...
I guess it is what it is.

596
00:36:14,880 --> 00:36:15,880
It is.

597
00:36:15,880 --> 00:36:18,080
It's the best way
for both of us to get there.

598
00:36:18,080 --> 00:36:19,120
Alright. Thanks.

599
00:36:22,240 --> 00:36:23,760
George isn't wrong.

600
00:36:23,760 --> 00:36:26,400
If I let Gerry fall on his sword,
it's the easy option.

601
00:36:26,400 --> 00:36:28,880
It guarantees me the top three.

602
00:36:30,240 --> 00:36:32,160
But Gerry's my closest ally
out here.

603
00:36:32,160 --> 00:36:36,160
And despite it's what he wants
this afternoon, I can't let him go.

604
00:36:37,160 --> 00:36:39,520
(SUSPENSEFUL MUSIC)

605
00:36:41,480 --> 00:36:45,680
Um, Gerry, me and George
just kind of agreed to vote you.

606
00:36:45,680 --> 00:36:48,560
However, I'm not gonna vote for you.
I'm only gonna vote for George.

607
00:36:49,560 --> 00:36:51,200
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

608
00:36:51,200 --> 00:36:52,960
It's the only way I can win.

609
00:36:52,960 --> 00:36:55,800
You can write that down whatever
you want to do. I'm just telling ya.

610
00:36:55,800 --> 00:36:59,080
I really don't want
to go to fire. Um...

611
00:36:59,080 --> 00:37:02,240
Sorry to...not...not
give you your wish.

612
00:37:02,240 --> 00:37:04,280
But that's just...
No. Well, let me think about it.

613
00:37:04,280 --> 00:37:06,680
Yeah, you can make up your mind
there and there's no pressure.

614
00:37:06,680 --> 00:37:09,080
You do what you want.
If I write you, I write you.

615
00:37:09,080 --> 00:37:11,120
Yep, that's fine. Yep.
OK.

616
00:37:12,280 --> 00:37:14,000
It's been a pleasure, Gerry.

617
00:37:14,000 --> 00:37:16,200
It's been an absolute pleasure
playing with you.

618
00:37:18,960 --> 00:37:20,880
(DARK MUSIC)

619
00:37:26,240 --> 00:37:28,880
So, what... What's the go?

620
00:37:28,880 --> 00:37:30,400
Are we doing it?

621
00:37:30,400 --> 00:37:32,280
I'm gonna vote for Gerry.
Yeah.

622
00:37:32,280 --> 00:37:34,000
Me and you vote for Gerry.

623
00:37:34,000 --> 00:37:37,240
And then the worst case,
I go to fire with Gerry.

624
00:37:39,120 --> 00:37:41,320
OK. Vote for Gerry.

625
00:37:41,320 --> 00:37:42,560
Yeah.

626
00:37:43,560 --> 00:37:45,920
I'll do whatever you want.
I'm voting Gerry.

627
00:37:45,920 --> 00:37:48,320
Thank you, Liz.
Love you, George.

628
00:37:53,840 --> 00:37:55,640
(INTENSE MUSIC)

629

GEORGE: Usually,
when I go into Tribal,

630
00:38:11,000 --> 00:38:12,480
I know the outcome.

631
00:38:12,480 --> 00:38:15,680
I know the numbers
because I've organised them.

632
00:38:16,680 --> 00:38:19,200
And tonight is exactly the same.

633
00:38:19,200 --> 00:38:23,880
Gerry, Matt and Liz,
they've never deviated away from me

634
00:38:23,880 --> 00:38:25,720
even when I blindsided them.

635
00:38:27,120 --> 00:38:28,880
The worst-case scenario,

636
00:38:28,880 --> 00:38:32,280
I'll have to beat Gerry
in a fire challenge to survive.

637
00:38:33,400 --> 00:38:36,120
But I'm confident
that Liz has my back tonight.

638
00:38:37,120 --> 00:38:40,240
I said, "Glory or death," on day 1

639
00:38:40,240 --> 00:38:44,560
and I reigned in a blaze of glory!

640
00:38:48,160 --> 00:38:49,640
That's why I'm the King.

641
00:38:49,640 --> 00:38:51,960
That's why I've gotten to the end

642
00:38:51,960 --> 00:38:53,760
And that's why I'm going to win.

643
00:38:59,120 --> 00:39:01,040
(SUBTLE MUSIC)

644
00:39:06,320 --> 00:39:07,320
(FLAMES WHOOSH)

645
00:39:07,320 --> 00:39:09,320
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

646
00:39:11,560 --> 00:39:12,720
GEORGE: Hello.

647
00:39:14,000 --> 00:39:15,320
(JONATHAN LAUGHS)
Afternoon.

648
00:39:15,320 --> 00:39:16,400
(CHUCKLES)

649
00:39:16,400 --> 00:39:19,120
(GERRY SPEAKS INDISTINCTLY)
Oh, it's back there, Gerry.

650
00:39:27,240 --> 00:39:29,200
We'll now bring in
the members of our jury.

651
00:39:31,880 --> 00:39:32,920
Flick.

652
00:39:32,920 --> 00:39:34,360
Sam.

653
00:39:34,360 --> 00:39:35,760
Shaun.

654
00:39:35,760 --> 00:39:37,480
Hayley.

655
00:39:37,480 --> 00:39:39,320
Simon.

656
00:39:39,320 --> 00:39:40,520
And Nina.

657
00:39:51,640 --> 00:39:54,800
So, Liz, I said it
at the challenge today

658
00:39:54,800 --> 00:39:56,680
and I'm going to say it again -

659
00:39:56,680 --> 00:39:59,800

for over four hours

660
00:39:59,800 --> 00:40:01,880

661
00:40:01,880 --> 00:40:04,840
How does it feel to be sitting here
wearing it tonight?

662
00:40:07,080 --> 00:40:09,560
Oh, I'm speechless, Jonathan.

663
00:40:09,560 --> 00:40:12,480
The challenge was pretty hectic,

664
00:40:12,480 --> 00:40:15,280
but having our families there,

665
00:40:15,280 --> 00:40:19,440
it was just, like,
all the motivation any of us needed.

666
00:40:19,440 --> 00:40:24,000
There was no way I was getting down
unless I literally fainted.

667
00:40:25,080 --> 00:40:28,440
Um, that's the kind of motivation

668
00:40:28,440 --> 00:40:31,160
that's been pushing Liz
throughout this game.

669
00:40:31,160 --> 00:40:35,240
And I've been really proud
to work with Liz since day 1

670
00:40:35,240 --> 00:40:37,080

671
00:40:37,080 --> 00:40:39,880
I like her frankness and directness.

672
00:40:39,880 --> 00:40:42,280
She brings joy to camp.

673
00:40:42,280 --> 00:40:46,200
But her strongest suit

674
00:40:46,200 --> 00:40:47,920
and she showed that today.

675
00:40:49,080 --> 00:40:52,480
Liz, George heaping
a lot of praise on you.

676
00:40:52,480 --> 00:40:54,080
I know!

677
00:40:54,080 --> 00:40:55,720
Thank you, George.

678
00:40:55,720 --> 00:40:57,960
Yes, I am driven.

679
00:40:57,960 --> 00:41:00,920
Today I knew I needed this necklace.

680
00:41:00,920 --> 00:41:06,120
The bond that these three boys have
is like a father and his sons.

681
00:41:06,120 --> 00:41:09,320
And I'm on the outside of that.

682
00:41:09,320 --> 00:41:13,400
So I knew that if I wanted to be
here tomorrow for final Tribal,

683
00:41:13,400 --> 00:41:14,920
I had to win.

684
00:41:14,920 --> 00:41:16,920
Because otherwise I was toast.

685
00:41:19,200 --> 00:41:21,920
So you honestly felt that
if you didn't take that necklace,

686
00:41:21,920 --> 00:41:23,640
you'd be walking down
that path tonight?

687
00:41:23,640 --> 00:41:25,480
110%.

688
00:41:28,920 --> 00:41:31,360
Well, Matt, you certainly
gave it everything today.

689
00:41:31,360 --> 00:41:34,320
Now that Liz has immunity,

690
00:41:34,320 --> 00:41:37,920
it is kind of
an interesting situation.

691
00:41:37,920 --> 00:41:39,880
You, George and Gerry,

692
00:41:39,880 --> 00:41:43,520
who have been super-tight
since the merge,

693
00:41:43,520 --> 00:41:46,120

but to vote for each other.

694
00:41:46,120 --> 00:41:47,280
(TENSE MUSIC)

695
00:41:47,280 --> 00:41:51,520
Um...yeah, definitely. One of us
is definitely going to the jury.

696
00:41:51,520 --> 00:41:54,360
And we need to be smart
about who that is.

697
00:41:57,880 --> 00:41:59,400
So, Gerry...

698
00:42:01,080 --> 00:42:03,720

for you

699
00:42:03,720 --> 00:42:06,560

your two closest allies?

700
00:42:07,560 --> 00:42:10,000
Yeah, it's a huge dilemma, Jonathan.

701
00:42:10,000 --> 00:42:13,680
I'm loyal to the both of them.

702
00:42:15,760 --> 00:42:20,760
Yeah, this is...this is the vote
that I didn't want to have to make.

703
00:42:20,760 --> 00:42:22,680
So, um... (SIGHS)

704
00:42:25,080 --> 00:42:28,480
..I'm stuck between the devil
and the deep blue sea.

705
00:42:28,480 --> 00:42:31,320
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

706
00:42:32,760 --> 00:42:36,400
Alright, well, I'm kind of curious
to see how it's gonna play out,

707
00:42:36,400 --> 00:42:39,120
so...it is...

708
00:42:39,120 --> 00:42:40,440
..time to vote.

709
00:42:47,000 --> 00:42:49,120
(TENSE MUSIC)

710
00:43:02,840 --> 00:43:06,360
Alright, well, I'm kind of curious
to see how it's going to play out,

711
00:43:06,360 --> 00:43:09,640
so...it is time to vote.

712
00:43:09,640 --> 00:43:11,280
Matt, you're up.

713
00:43:12,280 --> 00:43:14,160
(HAUNTING TRIBAL MUSIC)

714
00:43:50,600 --> 00:43:54,480
Gerry, it's been an absolute joy
to have played this game with you,

715
00:43:54,480 --> 00:43:59,160
but I need to send you to the jury
so I have a guaranteed vote

716
00:43:59,160 --> 00:44:01,360

717
00:44:01,360 --> 00:44:03,400
and that's what tonight
is about for me.

718
00:44:36,360 --> 00:44:37,760
(SIGHS)

719
00:45:09,640 --> 00:45:11,680
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

720
00:45:24,760 --> 00:45:27,040
I'll go count the votes.

721
00:45:48,960 --> 00:45:51,880
OK. I'll read the votes.

722
00:45:55,440 --> 00:45:58,160
First vote - George.

723
00:46:05,560 --> 00:46:06,560
Gerry.

724
00:46:07,560 --> 00:46:09,480
One vote George, one vote Gerry.

725
00:46:12,000 --> 00:46:14,240
(INTENSE MUSIC)

726
00:46:15,480 --> 00:46:16,600
George.

727
00:46:16,600 --> 00:46:20,480
Two votes George, one vote Gerry.

728
00:46:23,240 --> 00:46:24,480
One vote left.

729
00:46:32,280 --> 00:46:33,960
20th person voted out,

730
00:46:33,960 --> 00:46:37,240

731
00:46:38,480 --> 00:46:40,600
You need to bring me your torch.

732
00:46:41,600 --> 00:46:43,240
LIZ: Georgie!
It's been a pleasure, mate.

733
00:46:43,240 --> 00:46:44,240
All good.

734
00:46:45,320 --> 00:46:46,360
(SPEAKS INDISTINCTLY)

735
00:46:48,360 --> 00:46:50,440
Thanks, Gerry.
You alright?

736
00:46:54,000 --> 00:46:55,200
Liz.

737
00:46:55,200 --> 00:46:56,440
(WHISPERS)

738
00:46:57,880 --> 00:46:59,920
It's all good. Thanks, guys.

739
00:47:04,720 --> 00:47:08,520
Ohhh! It took you all 94 days
to do this.

740
00:47:08,520 --> 00:47:10,640
MATT: Yeah.
(LIZ CHUCKLES)

741
00:47:12,120 --> 00:47:14,480
Where do I put it?
Right there.

742
00:47:14,480 --> 00:47:15,520
(LAUGHS)

743
00:47:18,040 --> 00:47:19,920
George, the tribe has spoken.

744
00:47:28,760 --> 00:47:29,760
Good luck, guys.

745
00:47:29,760 --> 00:47:31,640
I'll see you all very soon.
See ya, mate!

746
00:47:31,640 --> 00:47:32,760
Well done.
Thanks, JLP.

747
00:47:32,760 --> 00:47:33,960
'Bye, George.

748
00:47:33,960 --> 00:47:36,280

749
00:47:41,880 --> 00:47:43,560
Congratulations.

750
00:47:43,560 --> 00:47:47,400
Liz, Matt and Gerry,
you are the Final Three.

751
00:47:47,400 --> 00:47:50,400
You've gone as far as you can go
in this game.

752
00:47:50,400 --> 00:47:54,240
Tomorrow night,
now the power shifts to the jury.

753
00:47:54,240 --> 00:47:57,920
So I suggest go back to camp,
get some rest

754
00:47:57,920 --> 00:48:00,080

how you're gonna convince them

755
00:48:00,080 --> 00:48:02,080
that you deserve the title
of Sole Survivor

756
00:48:02,080 --> 00:48:04,280
and the half-million dollars
that goes with it.

757
00:48:04,280 --> 00:48:07,200
Well done.
Grab your torches. Head on out.

758
00:48:07,200 --> 00:48:09,200
Thanks, Jonathan.
Thanks, Jonathan.

759
00:48:23,440 --> 00:48:25,440

760
00:48:32,800 --> 00:48:34,720
GERRY: Last day in paradise.

761
00:48:34,720 --> 00:48:36,520
MATT: Last day

762
00:48:36,520 --> 00:48:39,040

763
00:48:40,480 --> 00:48:43,560
There's three parts on that sign.
It says outwit, outplay and outlast.

764
00:48:43,560 --> 00:48:45,000
Did the lot.

765
00:48:45,000 --> 00:48:46,880
What an honour

766
00:48:46,880 --> 00:48:48,880
to be the Final Three.

767
00:48:48,880 --> 00:48:52,520
Ohh, man! Let's have a great day.

768
00:48:52,520 --> 00:48:54,640
Let's have a good day.
Let's have a good day.

769
00:48:55,920 --> 00:48:57,400

770
00:48:57,400 --> 00:49:01,680
I sent King George
to the jury bench.

771
00:49:03,360 --> 00:49:05,880
It was difficult for me

772

really closely

773
00:49:07,840 --> 00:49:10,480

774
00:49:10,480 --> 00:49:12,120
But...

775
00:49:12,120 --> 00:49:14,000
..this is revenge for Shonee.

776
00:49:15,160 --> 00:49:19,040
I have been waiting for the
perfect moment to take George out.

777
00:49:19,040 --> 00:49:21,800
I've had to put my emotions aside.

778
00:49:22,800 --> 00:49:25,440
I'm so proud that
I'm the last villain standing.

779
00:49:26,640 --> 00:49:29,960
I'm so proud that
I'm the last female standing.

780
00:49:33,400 --> 00:49:37,240
Everyone on that jury
is a second-time player.

781
00:49:37,240 --> 00:49:38,720
Oh!
We're all newbies.

782
00:49:38,720 --> 00:49:40,160
Yeah, we're all first-timers.
Yeah.

783
00:49:40,160 --> 00:49:43,680
I'm really nervous about
facing the jury tonight.

784
00:49:43,680 --> 00:49:48,160
The jury bench
is majority OG Heroes.

785
00:49:48,160 --> 00:49:50,000
Should we go swimming?
Let's go.

786
00:49:50,000 --> 00:49:51,840
Let's go.

787
00:49:51,840 --> 00:49:55,000
Gerry, he has a great story.

788
00:49:57,040 --> 00:50:01,720
Matt, on the other hand,
he is a golden boy.

789
00:50:04,000 --> 00:50:05,840
So, tonight,

790
00:50:05,840 --> 00:50:09,440

who can sell their story the best.

791
00:50:18,200 --> 00:50:19,680
Orange juice and milk!
There's juice!

792
00:50:20,760 --> 00:50:23,520
Oh, let's have a looksies here, eh?

793
00:50:23,520 --> 00:50:25,440
(READS) "Congratulations!

794
00:50:25,440 --> 00:50:27,720
"You have made it
to the Final Three.

795
00:50:27,720 --> 00:50:31,720
"Enjoy your well-earnt
day 47 Survivor breakfast!"

796
00:50:31,720 --> 00:50:33,440
Whoo!
Whoo!

797
00:50:33,440 --> 00:50:35,720
Congratulations.
Oh!

798
00:50:35,720 --> 00:50:37,920
We did it!
We did.

799
00:50:37,920 --> 00:50:39,440
Let's feast!

800
00:50:39,440 --> 00:50:42,680
It's a surreal feeling. I never
thought I'd make it this far.

801
00:50:42,680 --> 00:50:44,160
(LAUGHS)
(CORK POPS)

802
00:50:44,160 --> 00:50:45,640
Yay!

803
00:50:45,640 --> 00:50:46,720
Oh, quick, quick, quick, quick!

804
00:50:46,720 --> 00:50:50,160
It is a privilege to be here

805
00:50:50,160 --> 00:50:51,600
The Final Three.

806
00:50:51,600 --> 00:50:55,320
And we're fighting it out
to become Sole Survivor.

807
00:50:55,320 --> 00:50:57,720
Cheers to being the Final Three.

808
00:50:57,720 --> 00:50:59,480
To the top three!

809
00:50:59,480 --> 00:51:00,840
Congratulations.
Thanks, guys.

810
00:51:00,840 --> 00:51:01,880
Beautiful.

811
00:51:01,880 --> 00:51:03,600

812
00:51:05,360 --> 00:51:09,360
I sacrificed a long being out here,

813
00:51:09,360 --> 00:51:11,200
But I'm here doing it for them.

814
00:51:13,840 --> 00:51:16,800
A one-in-three shot

815
00:51:16,800 --> 00:51:19,680
is the closest I'm ever gonna get

816
00:51:19,680 --> 00:51:22,400
and I'm not gonna waste
this opportunity.

817
00:51:22,400 --> 00:51:25,240
Alright, coffee's brewin'.
Thanks for that, Gerry.

818
00:51:25,240 --> 00:51:26,320
Look at that!

819
00:51:26,320 --> 00:51:28,680
Whoo!
Whoo-hoo!

820
00:51:28,680 --> 00:51:30,000
Fire!

821
00:51:30,000 --> 00:51:31,680

822
00:51:31,680 --> 00:51:33,120
Look at that, Gerry.

823
00:51:33,120 --> 00:51:34,240
Oh.

824
00:51:34,240 --> 00:51:35,600
Whoa!

825
00:51:35,600 --> 00:51:38,560
GERRY: Coming into this game,
in my wildest dreams,

826
00:51:38,560 --> 00:51:40,360
I never thought that
I'd get to the end.

827
00:51:40,360 --> 00:51:42,480
I've done it.

828
00:51:42,480 --> 00:51:43,880
I've done it!

829
00:51:43,880 --> 00:51:46,440
Little brother.
Thank you, big brother.

830
00:51:46,440 --> 00:51:48,040

831
00:51:48,040 --> 00:51:51,760
I am the oldest player

832
00:51:51,760 --> 00:51:54,080

833
00:51:54,080 --> 00:51:57,720
I've proved old dogs
learn new tricks.

834
00:51:59,520 --> 00:52:02,000
Winning half a million dollars

835
00:52:02,000 --> 00:52:06,040
would actually change my entire life.

836
00:52:07,040 --> 00:52:12,080
(TEARFULLY) My whole life
has been des...destroyed by COVID.

837
00:52:12,080 --> 00:52:13,160

838
00:52:13,160 --> 00:52:14,400

839
00:52:16,080 --> 00:52:17,720
My business...

840
00:52:18,920 --> 00:52:20,160
..destroyed.

841
00:52:21,240 --> 00:52:24,400
This money would give back
to my family...

842
00:52:26,320 --> 00:52:28,160
..what I feel that I've lost.

843
00:52:29,960 --> 00:52:31,280
(SNIFFLES)

844
00:52:31,280 --> 00:52:32,880
This would get us back on track.

845
00:52:41,160 --> 00:52:42,960
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

846
00:52:50,560 --> 00:52:54,160
Tonight,
I need to get my pitch right.

847
00:52:54,160 --> 00:52:57,200
I need to get my story
across the line,

848
00:52:57,200 --> 00:52:59,880
because these people
that are on the jury,

849
00:52:59,880 --> 00:53:01,480
I put them there.

850
00:53:01,480 --> 00:53:03,120
I voted them out.

851
00:53:03,120 --> 00:53:05,040
I've got to turn them around.

852
00:53:06,200 --> 00:53:08,240
There can only be one winner.

853
00:53:08,240 --> 00:53:10,040
Only one.

854
00:53:10,040 --> 00:53:11,920
I want it to be me.

855
00:53:22,000 --> 00:53:25,160

856
00:53:31,160 --> 00:53:32,400
(FLAMES WHOOSH)

857
00:54:02,000 --> 00:54:03,600

858
00:54:05,480 --> 00:54:07,560
We'll now bring in
the members of our jury.

859
00:54:08,800 --> 00:54:09,800
Flick.

860
00:54:09,800 --> 00:54:10,920
Sam.

861
00:54:10,920 --> 00:54:12,120
Shaun.

862
00:54:12,120 --> 00:54:13,560
Hayley.

863
00:54:13,560 --> 00:54:14,920
Simon.

864
00:54:14,920 --> 00:54:16,120
Nina.

865
00:54:16,120 --> 00:54:17,720
And George.

866
00:54:18,720 --> 00:54:20,840
Voted out at the last Tribal Council.
(LAUGHS)

867
00:54:21,840 --> 00:54:24,000
Look at your face! (LAUGHS)

868
00:54:24,000 --> 00:54:26,240
MATT: That's a moustache!

869
00:54:27,440 --> 00:54:28,960

870
00:54:28,960 --> 00:54:32,800
OK, so...here we are,

871
00:54:32,800 --> 00:54:36,880

872
00:54:37,920 --> 00:54:40,200
Two heroes and one villain,

873
00:54:40,200 --> 00:54:42,720
you've gone as far as you can
in this game

874
00:54:42,720 --> 00:54:45,840
and tonight,
the power shifts to the jury.

875
00:54:47,080 --> 00:54:49,720
Seven people you've had a hand
in voting out,

876
00:54:49,720 --> 00:54:51,600

877
00:54:51,600 --> 00:54:55,760
will now decide which of you three
deserves the title of Sole Survivor

878
00:54:55,760 --> 00:54:58,240
and the half-million dollars
that goes with it.

879
00:55:01,360 --> 00:55:03,160
Here's how it's gonna work.

880
00:55:03,160 --> 00:55:05,760
You'll each make
an opening statement.

881
00:55:05,760 --> 00:55:08,960
This is your chance
to pitch to the jury

882
00:55:08,960 --> 00:55:12,200
why you think you deserve
to win this game.

883
00:55:12,200 --> 00:55:13,920
Then the jury will address you.

884
00:55:13,920 --> 00:55:17,080
They'll ask you questions
and you'll answer them.

885
00:55:17,080 --> 00:55:19,200
Once everyone's had their say,

886
00:55:19,200 --> 00:55:21,280
the jury will then go up to vote

887
00:55:21,280 --> 00:55:25,400
to decide who wins Australian
Survivor Heroes v Villains.

888
00:55:29,920 --> 00:55:34,080
Alright, Liz...
would you like to kick us off?

889
00:55:44,600 --> 00:55:48,600
I came into the game of Survivor
as a physical threat

890
00:55:48,600 --> 00:55:50,960
being a two-time Olympian.

891
00:55:50,960 --> 00:55:53,160
I won the Reward Challenge
for the Villains

892
00:55:53,160 --> 00:55:54,840
when the boys couldn't pull through.

893
00:55:54,840 --> 00:56:00,520
I won the day spa reward and I won
three individual immunity necklaces.

894
00:56:01,520 --> 00:56:03,600
Last night's necklace
was the most important

895
00:56:03,600 --> 00:56:06,480
because it put me on this bench
tonight to pitch to you all.

896
00:56:08,760 --> 00:56:11,680
Even though I came into this game
as a clear challenge beast,

897
00:56:11,680 --> 00:56:15,280
I had no experience
in my strategic game.

898
00:56:15,280 --> 00:56:18,080
I had to lean on returning players

899
00:56:18,080 --> 00:56:22,360
such as George, Simon, Shonee
and Jordie from the Villains

900
00:56:22,360 --> 00:56:25,520
to absorb their information,
to absorb their strategy,

901
00:56:25,520 --> 00:56:28,600
and make it my own
strategic powerhouse.

902
00:56:29,920 --> 00:56:34,400
I had multiple alliances
throughout this game at once.

903
00:56:34,400 --> 00:56:37,640
I had the Shiz alliance,
I had the Spice Girls,

904
00:56:37,640 --> 00:56:39,760
I had the Vigilantes

905
00:56:39,760 --> 00:56:42,040
and I had the Jacuzzi alliance.

906
00:56:42,040 --> 00:56:44,440
In order to have
all of these alliances,

907
00:56:44,440 --> 00:56:47,520
I had to make genuine connections
with all of you.

908
00:56:48,640 --> 00:56:52,040
And that is why even thought I have
voted for many of you on that bench,

909
00:56:52,040 --> 00:56:56,120
I never burnt those bridges
and I kept you on my side.

910
00:56:56,120 --> 00:56:58,960
My final point for this evening

911
00:56:58,960 --> 00:57:01,400
is the take-down of King George.

912
00:57:02,960 --> 00:57:06,440
Georgie Pie, you have played
an incredible game.

913
00:57:07,520 --> 00:57:09,160
But when you crossed me,

914
00:57:09,160 --> 00:57:12,880
I made it my mission to make sure
that I came after you.

915
00:57:12,880 --> 00:57:15,280
You took Shonee away from me.

916
00:57:15,280 --> 00:57:17,160
You took Shonee off the jury bench

917
00:57:17,160 --> 00:57:19,840
'cause you knew that if I was
sitting here, that was my vote.

918
00:57:19,840 --> 00:57:22,880
And then you took Nina away from me.

919
00:57:22,880 --> 00:57:25,600
And that broke up
the Jacuzzi alliance.

920
00:57:26,600 --> 00:57:31,640
I put my emotions to the side
and I thought about strategy,

921
00:57:31,640 --> 00:57:34,040
and I thought, "Right,
if I'm gonna take George down,

922
00:57:34,040 --> 00:57:35,640
"this has to be the perfect moment,"

923
00:57:35,640 --> 00:57:38,360
and you know
when that moment was, George?

924
00:57:38,360 --> 00:57:40,880
That was last night.

925
00:57:43,280 --> 00:57:46,040
Many of you have tried
to take George down,

926
00:57:46,040 --> 00:57:49,120
but I did that, that was my move.

927
00:57:51,560 --> 00:57:54,960
I'm so proud of myself
and what I have achieved

928
00:57:54,960 --> 00:57:56,600
and the hurdles that I've overcome.

929
00:57:56,600 --> 00:58:00,880
And no matter what happens tonight,
I'm a winner

930
00:58:00,880 --> 00:58:04,040
because this whole experience
has changed my life.

931
00:58:08,040 --> 00:58:11,800
Alright. Matt, now it's your shot.

932
00:58:13,280 --> 00:58:14,560
Jury.

933
00:58:15,600 --> 00:58:18,800
I came into this game as a lifeguard

934
00:58:18,800 --> 00:58:22,640
with a hope that I could transform
my family's life.

935
00:58:22,640 --> 00:58:25,240
So I'm gonna start
with my social game.

936
00:58:25,240 --> 00:58:28,680
I took time to get to know
each and every person

937
00:58:28,680 --> 00:58:32,720
because social connections
is the currency of this game.

938
00:58:33,960 --> 00:58:35,840
Tribe swap.

939
00:58:35,840 --> 00:58:38,520
I had to take my social game
to another level to survive.

940
00:58:38,520 --> 00:58:41,840
That night where I sat here
and I pitched for my life.

941
00:58:42,840 --> 00:58:46,200
The time I put in with George
to make myself more valuable

942
00:58:46,200 --> 00:58:49,640
than one of your own
got me through that night.

943
00:58:49,640 --> 00:58:52,320
My social game was then reflected
in my strategy.

944
00:58:52,320 --> 00:58:56,360
The moment where I gave
my phone call away to Jordie

945
00:58:56,360 --> 00:58:59,440
was the hardest thing by a mile
I'd done in this game.

946
00:59:02,040 --> 00:59:04,360
Giving up that opportunity
to talk to my wife,

947
00:59:04,360 --> 00:59:07,400
to find out that...
that our little baby was OK.

948
00:59:08,400 --> 00:59:11,400
In a selfish game, I had
the opportunity to be selfless.

949
00:59:14,080 --> 00:59:18,200
But what it did actually do
was amongst everyone of us here

950
00:59:18,200 --> 00:59:20,280
it elevated my game as a nice guy.

951
00:59:20,280 --> 00:59:22,880
No-one suspected me
when it came to merge

952
00:59:22,880 --> 00:59:24,720
that I would be the person to flip.

953
00:59:26,080 --> 00:59:30,200
I would take the opportunity to...to
move from being probably the bottom

954
00:59:30,200 --> 00:59:32,000
of the OG Heroes

955
00:59:32,000 --> 00:59:35,520
to being an integral part
of the new Vigilantes alliance.

956
00:59:35,520 --> 00:59:37,000
And that's what I did.

957
00:59:37,000 --> 00:59:38,800
And in that Vigilantes alliance,

958
00:59:38,800 --> 00:59:42,600
we had a secret three
of George, Gerry and myself.

959
00:59:43,600 --> 00:59:46,880
My other attribute that I brought
into this game was my physical game.

960
00:59:46,880 --> 00:59:50,080
I won three immunity necklaces
and an extra vote.

961
00:59:51,800 --> 00:59:55,640
When you guys are thinking about who
do you want to best represent you,

962
00:59:55,640 --> 00:59:59,480
I hope the all-round game
of my social strength, my strategy

963
00:59:59,480 --> 01:00:03,800
and my physical game can
best represent us as a whole

964
01:00:03,800 --> 01:00:05,360
as the Heroes v Villains.

965
01:00:05,360 --> 01:00:06,680
Thanks, guys.

966
01:00:10,160 --> 01:00:13,480
Alright, Gerry,
you want to bring us home?

967
01:00:13,480 --> 01:00:18,680
Jury members, I know I usually have
long-winded stories.

968
01:00:18,680 --> 01:00:21,960
Tonight is going to be
short and sweet.

969
01:00:21,960 --> 01:00:26,120
I came into this game
the oldest person

970
01:00:26,120 --> 01:00:28,880
ever to play Australian Survivor.

971
01:00:28,880 --> 01:00:33,480
We know what happens to the oldest
people that come into this game.

972
01:00:33,480 --> 01:00:36,160
They're usually voted out first.

973
01:00:37,160 --> 01:00:38,680
I'm still here.

974
01:00:39,720 --> 01:00:43,440
I succumbed to injury
in the first week of this game.

975
01:00:44,440 --> 01:00:49,080
I should have been voted off
right there and then.

976
01:00:49,080 --> 01:00:51,080
I'm still here.

977
01:00:51,080 --> 01:00:55,240
And then...I was cast
to the other side.

978
01:00:56,720 --> 01:01:00,680
Deemed disposable
by my fellow tribe members.

979
01:01:03,080 --> 01:01:05,360
I had work to do!

980
01:01:05,360 --> 01:01:08,440
My game had to change -

981
01:01:08,440 --> 01:01:12,080
change quickly and viciously.

982
01:01:12,080 --> 01:01:13,760
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

983
01:01:14,840 --> 01:01:19,440
By sending me over there,
you flicked a switch in my head

984
01:01:19,440 --> 01:01:21,200
and I turned on you!

985
01:01:21,200 --> 01:01:25,040
Because I was just a number
for you to vote out.

986
01:01:25,040 --> 01:01:31,160
So, the top five in the OG Heroes
became my hit list.

987
01:01:34,040 --> 01:01:40,920
George, he is arguably the best
strategic game player of Survivor.

988
01:01:40,920 --> 01:01:45,880
I wanted that man on my team
and I got him.

989
01:01:45,880 --> 01:01:49,080
We teamed up as partners.

990
01:01:49,080 --> 01:01:52,560
So, we knocked everybody off
one by one.

991
01:01:52,560 --> 01:01:54,280
The stats don't lie.

992
01:01:54,280 --> 01:01:59,240
Every time I voted for somebody,
hit the mark.

993
01:01:59,240 --> 01:02:02,480
I played this game
to the best of my ability,

994
01:02:02,480 --> 01:02:04,280
as hard as I possibly can,

995
01:02:04,280 --> 01:02:05,840
my way.

996
01:02:11,760 --> 01:02:15,600
Alright, jury,
you've heard three great pitches.

997
01:02:15,600 --> 01:02:18,480
Now it's your turn to ask questions.

998
01:02:18,480 --> 01:02:19,960
Remember, you're looking
for information

999
01:02:19,960 --> 01:02:23,000
to help you make
a half-million-dollar decision.

1000
01:02:23,000 --> 01:02:25,160
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

1001
01:02:28,000 --> 01:02:29,840
(THUNDER CRACKS)

1002
01:02:37,920 --> 01:02:41,840
(THUNDER CRACKS)

1003
01:03:01,400 --> 01:03:05,240
Alright, jury,
you've heard three great pitches.

1004
01:03:05,240 --> 01:03:07,920
Now it's your turn to ask questions.

1005
01:03:07,920 --> 01:03:09,520
Remember, you're looking
for information

1006
01:03:09,520 --> 01:03:12,640
to help you make
a half-million-dollar decision.

1007
01:03:12,640 --> 01:03:14,600
(THUNDER RUMBLES, RAIN PATTERS)

1008
01:03:14,600 --> 01:03:17,440
Alright, Sam, do you have questions?
Yeah, mate, I do.

1009
01:03:19,240 --> 01:03:23,360
Congratulations,
my fellow tribemates.

1010
01:03:23,360 --> 01:03:26,240
I've got one question for you, Liz.
Yeah.

1011
01:03:26,240 --> 01:03:29,440
How did you play this game
proactively

1012
01:03:29,440 --> 01:03:31,600
as opposed to reactively?

1013
01:03:31,600 --> 01:03:34,000
Great question.
It's a great question.

1014
01:03:35,960 --> 01:03:38,840
I played this game proactively

1015
01:03:38,840 --> 01:03:41,560
from the moment I landed
at the beach.

1016
01:03:41,560 --> 01:03:44,040
I had to hit the ground running

1017
01:03:44,040 --> 01:03:46,240
because otherwise
I would have been left behind

1018
01:03:46,240 --> 01:03:48,280
by all you returning players.

1019
01:03:49,280 --> 01:03:50,840
And then for the tribe swap,

1020
01:03:50,840 --> 01:03:53,440
I was outnumbered by OG Heroes

1021
01:03:53,440 --> 01:03:55,520
and it was sink or swim.

1022
01:03:55,520 --> 01:03:58,400
And I managed to stay afloat.

1023
01:03:58,400 --> 01:04:02,120
I put all the skills that
I had learnt into practice.

1024
01:04:02,120 --> 01:04:04,360
I formed a new alliance.

1025
01:04:04,360 --> 01:04:06,400
I got to mutiny
and I made it across

1026
01:04:06,400 --> 01:04:09,080
back to my original alliance.

1027
01:04:09,080 --> 01:04:10,600
And I'm bloody proud of that.

1028
01:04:11,640 --> 01:04:13,440
Thank you.
Thank you.

1029
01:04:16,040 --> 01:04:18,800
SIMON: Gerry, I have a...
a question for you.

1030
01:04:20,240 --> 01:04:23,120
I'd like you to explain why

1031
01:04:23,120 --> 01:04:26,080
you believe you had control
over your game.

1032
01:04:26,080 --> 01:04:28,880
I was under the presumption that

1033
01:04:28,880 --> 01:04:31,480
you were being controlled
and manipulated

1034
01:04:31,480 --> 01:04:34,200
by George, in particular.

1035
01:04:36,280 --> 01:04:37,920
No! That's not true.

1036
01:04:38,920 --> 01:04:44,400
I know to succeed in this game,
you cannot do it all yourself.

1037
01:04:45,400 --> 01:04:47,000
I wasn't George's pawn.

1038
01:04:47,000 --> 01:04:50,360
We were both driving
this ship together.

1039
01:04:50,360 --> 01:04:53,840
I actually turned George around...

1040
01:04:55,240 --> 01:04:57,280
..right here on these seats.

1041
01:04:59,320 --> 01:05:01,360
This is George we're talking about.

1042
01:05:01,360 --> 01:05:04,480
That's the power of our connection.

1043
01:05:06,960 --> 01:05:08,680
Is that not right, George?

1044
01:05:09,760 --> 01:05:11,440
It's true.

1045
01:05:15,360 --> 01:05:19,320
George, would you like
to ask them something?

1046
01:05:19,320 --> 01:05:20,480
Thanks, Jonathan.

1047
01:05:20,480 --> 01:05:22,680
I just wanna congratulate
the three of you

1048
01:05:22,680 --> 01:05:24,720
because I know how hard
and how nerve-racking it is

1049
01:05:24,720 --> 01:05:26,240
to make a pitch here,

1050
01:05:26,240 --> 01:05:29,080
and the difficult thing for me
tonight is this -

1051
01:05:29,080 --> 01:05:32,760
the three of you were
my three closest allies in the game.

1052
01:05:32,760 --> 01:05:35,040
And all three of you are my friends.

1053
01:05:35,040 --> 01:05:37,400
But I've got to set friendship aside

1054
01:05:37,400 --> 01:05:39,720
and I've got to vote for one of you.

1055
01:05:39,720 --> 01:05:41,440
(TENSE MUSIC)

1056
01:05:41,440 --> 01:05:43,640
I do have a question

1057
01:05:43,640 --> 01:05:47,280
and it's the same question
for both Liz and Matt.

1058
01:05:47,280 --> 01:05:49,360
What I want to know from both of you

1059
01:05:49,360 --> 01:05:53,600
is what move did you make
that wasn't instigated by me?

1060
01:06:00,920 --> 01:06:04,160
I know Liz claimed the vote
to vote you off, George,

1061
01:06:04,160 --> 01:06:07,440
but yesterday,
I'd pulled Gerry aside

1062
01:06:07,440 --> 01:06:09,840
and I said that I was voting George.

1063
01:06:11,560 --> 01:06:13,000
Uh, no.

1064
01:06:17,360 --> 01:06:19,880
Matt, you say that you were
instrumental in that vote

1065
01:06:19,880 --> 01:06:22,080
and I have to disagree.

1066
01:06:23,200 --> 01:06:26,640
The idea for me started
when George took out Shonee.

1067
01:06:28,240 --> 01:06:30,280
Amidst all this heartbreak,

1068
01:06:30,280 --> 01:06:32,680
I knew the only way
for me to take him out

1069
01:06:32,680 --> 01:06:35,080
is to stay socially close to him,

1070
01:06:35,080 --> 01:06:38,160
to make him believe
that we were together.

1071
01:06:38,160 --> 01:06:40,800
And I outwitted and I outplayed

1072
01:06:40,800 --> 01:06:43,280
because I kept that information
to myself.

1073
01:06:43,280 --> 01:06:46,520
I knew George's strength
in his strategy

1074
01:06:46,520 --> 01:06:48,200
that he was getting to the end.

1075
01:06:48,200 --> 01:06:50,200
I waited and I waited,

1076
01:06:50,200 --> 01:06:54,280
and when the moment was perfect,
at the final hour,

1077
01:06:54,280 --> 01:06:57,040
George, I had to send you
to that bench.

1078
01:06:59,960 --> 01:07:03,280
Can I add something, Jonathan?
Absolutely. Go for it.

1079
01:07:03,280 --> 01:07:05,280
I actually did have a moment.

1080
01:07:05,280 --> 01:07:08,720
I was worried that you had flipped
with the girls

1081
01:07:08,720 --> 01:07:10,880
and that's when I was actually,
honestly, Simon,

1082
01:07:10,880 --> 01:07:13,760
really considering working with you
after the Hayley vote.

1083
01:07:13,760 --> 01:07:15,400
And I went to Gerry and I said,

1084
01:07:15,400 --> 01:07:18,320
"Gerry, we have an opportunity
right now. We can take out George."

1085
01:07:18,320 --> 01:07:21,080
However, moving forward,
we still trusted George,

1086
01:07:21,080 --> 01:07:23,680
so we stayed with him
and didn't act on it.

1087
01:07:23,680 --> 01:07:25,000
But that was actually a plan.

1088
01:07:27,680 --> 01:07:28,680
So, thank you.

1089
01:07:28,680 --> 01:07:31,720
Matt, a move can't be an idea.
It had to happen.

1090
01:07:31,720 --> 01:07:35,680
There's...there's no ifs here.
We want to know your move.

1091
01:07:35,680 --> 01:07:38,120
(TENSE MUSIC)

1092
01:07:40,240 --> 01:07:45,440
When, um, we sent Nina...
or when Nina and Gerry...

1093
01:07:45,440 --> 01:07:48,360
I sent Nina...next to me.
Yes.

1094
01:07:48,360 --> 01:07:50,720
What was your move in this game?

1095
01:07:50,720 --> 01:07:53,200
(TENSE MUSIC BUILDS)

1096
01:07:53,200 --> 01:07:56,360
I don't want to hear how
you participated in my moves.

1097
01:07:56,360 --> 01:07:59,400
I'm happy to vote for you.
Just tell me what your move was.

1098
01:08:03,440 --> 01:08:06,400
Can I make a comment?
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

1099
01:08:11,000 --> 01:08:13,000
JONATHAN: Want to win
a top-of-the-range Isuzu D-MAX

1100
01:08:13,000 --> 01:08:14,120
or MU-X?

1101
01:08:14,120 --> 01:08:16,600
Head to the 10 play Win page now

1102
01:08:16,600 --> 01:08:18,160
for all the details.

1103
01:08:20,000 --> 01:08:22,240
(UNSETTLING MUSIC)

1104
01:08:29,320 --> 01:08:32,360
I don't want to hear how
you participated in my moves.

1105
01:08:32,360 --> 01:08:35,520
I'm happy to vote for you.
Just tell me what your move was.

1106
01:08:41,920 --> 01:08:44,040
Can I make a comment?
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

1107
01:08:44,040 --> 01:08:46,720
George, there was many moments

1108
01:08:46,720 --> 01:08:50,680
that Shonee and I were behind
the scenes working against you

1109
01:08:50,680 --> 01:08:54,480
and you didn't know that
because we played a witty game.

1110
01:08:54,480 --> 01:08:56,280
We played it smart.

1111
01:08:57,280 --> 01:09:00,240
We kept our cards
close to our chest.

1112
01:09:00,240 --> 01:09:03,560
I saved Flick that night
when you wanted to put her down

1113
01:09:03,560 --> 01:09:05,760
and I said,
"George, I'll play my idol for her,"

1114
01:09:05,760 --> 01:09:08,040
and you said,
"OK, we'll swap the vote."

1115
01:09:10,000 --> 01:09:11,600
It's true.

1116
01:09:12,600 --> 01:09:16,080
I may be fierce, I may be sassy,
I may be blunt, and black and white,

1117
01:09:16,080 --> 01:09:17,960
but I don't waver.

1118
01:09:19,480 --> 01:09:24,600
George, on multiple occasions,
I questioned you, I rebutted you.

1119
01:09:25,600 --> 01:09:27,480
And when it was time to strike,

1120
01:09:27,480 --> 01:09:30,480
I hit it and I got you
on that jury bench.

1121
01:09:41,520 --> 01:09:43,720
Alright.

1122
01:09:43,720 --> 01:09:44,800
Hayley.

1123
01:09:45,800 --> 01:09:47,520
Congratulations to the three of you.

1124
01:09:47,520 --> 01:09:49,840
It is no small feat
to get to where you are.

1125
01:09:49,840 --> 01:09:51,600
You should all be very proud.

1126
01:09:52,600 --> 01:09:56,280
Gerry, self-reflection
and self-awareness

1127
01:09:56,280 --> 01:09:59,200
is really important to me
in this game.

1128
01:09:59,200 --> 01:10:03,640
Is there anything that you've done,
strategically or socially,

1129
01:10:03,640 --> 01:10:04,880
that you regret?

1130
01:10:07,200 --> 01:10:12,400
Any decisions that I've made in this
game, I don't regret any of them.

1131
01:10:12,400 --> 01:10:16,360
My social game...
I played differently.

1132
01:10:17,760 --> 01:10:20,920
We have a huge...age gap.

1133
01:10:20,920 --> 01:10:22,680
Over 30 years.

1134
01:10:22,680 --> 01:10:25,280
Because of such a huge age gap...

1135
01:10:26,560 --> 01:10:29,160
..I couldn't really connect...

1136
01:10:30,200 --> 01:10:33,920
..on your level the way I wanted to.

1137
01:10:35,560 --> 01:10:38,800
Football was big with you guys.

1138
01:10:38,800 --> 01:10:41,600
I know nothing about football.

1139
01:10:41,600 --> 01:10:43,800
We are so differently wired.

1140
01:10:45,000 --> 01:10:47,160
To bring that together as one...

1141
01:10:48,440 --> 01:10:50,640
..is a feat in itself.

1142
01:10:51,640 --> 01:10:53,960
Gerry, you mention
your social game...

1143
01:10:53,960 --> 01:10:54,960
Mmm.

1144
01:10:54,960 --> 01:10:59,080
..maybe being at odds to us because
there is a 30-year difference.

1145
01:10:59,080 --> 01:11:00,080
Yeah.

1146
01:11:00,080 --> 01:11:04,000
But I think at the end of the day,
it's still human interaction.

1147
01:11:04,000 --> 01:11:06,680
And I know from my point of view

1148
01:11:06,680 --> 01:11:11,120
that I felt like it was
genuinely a one-way street.

1149
01:11:12,120 --> 01:11:13,600
It was always about you.

1150
01:11:17,640 --> 01:11:19,400
Mate, I'll add to that as well.

1151
01:11:19,400 --> 01:11:21,200
I mean, you mentioned
football was the talk.

1152
01:11:21,200 --> 01:11:23,400
Dave and I both played football
professionally.

1153
01:11:23,400 --> 01:11:25,280
Yeah.
And that something we had in common.

1154
01:11:25,280 --> 01:11:26,280
Yeah.

1155
01:11:26,280 --> 01:11:28,880
That was something that I rarely
talked about unless it was with him

1156
01:11:28,880 --> 01:11:30,440
or asked about.

1157
01:11:30,440 --> 01:11:33,560
Football was a job.
It's not a hobby of mine.

1158
01:11:33,560 --> 01:11:35,640
Do you know my hobbies?

1159
01:11:37,000 --> 01:11:38,640
No, I don't.
Yeah.

1160
01:11:38,640 --> 01:11:41,480
I know yours
and some of ours matched up.

1161
01:11:41,480 --> 01:11:43,840
I love hiking,
I love climbing mountains and stuff.

1162
01:11:43,840 --> 01:11:46,640
But you made assumptions
and you didn't take the time.

1163
01:11:46,640 --> 01:11:48,200
I think that's the issue.

1164
01:11:48,200 --> 01:11:49,680
Fair enough. OK.

1165
01:11:49,680 --> 01:11:52,760
If that's...a mistake I made...

1166
01:11:54,840 --> 01:11:56,360
..I can't apologise for that.

1167
01:12:00,440 --> 01:12:03,240
I am who I am.
(THUNDER RUMBLES)

1168
01:12:10,040 --> 01:12:12,960
HAYLEY: Very soon we're gonna walk
down that path and write down a name

1169
01:12:12,960 --> 01:12:15,120
and it will change your life,

1170
01:12:15,120 --> 01:12:18,040
and I know that 'cause
I've had great opportunity myself.

1171
01:12:18,040 --> 01:12:20,400
Um...and I don't take that lightly.

1172
01:12:20,400 --> 01:12:22,440
So I need you to keep fighting

1173
01:12:22,440 --> 01:12:26,840
and tell me why I should give you
my vote to win tonight.

1174
01:12:26,840 --> 01:12:28,520
(GERRY CLEARS THROAT)

1175
01:12:28,520 --> 01:12:32,120
I came into this game
behind the eight ball.

1176
01:12:33,120 --> 01:12:35,440
Here I am, 47 days later.

1177
01:12:35,440 --> 01:12:37,360
This game...

1178
01:12:38,560 --> 01:12:42,400
..has given me
a 64-year new lease of life.

1179
01:12:47,280 --> 01:12:50,720
I'm proud of who I am.
I'm proud of what I've done.

1180
01:12:50,720 --> 01:12:52,640
Nobody can take that away from me.

1181
01:12:55,320 --> 01:12:57,200
I'm a winner!

1182
01:12:58,240 --> 01:13:00,040
Whether you vote for me or not.

1183
01:13:08,720 --> 01:13:12,600
LIZ: I wanted to come into this game
and be bold and take risks

1184
01:13:12,600 --> 01:13:14,120
and just YOLO it.

1185
01:13:14,120 --> 01:13:17,160
And I did that.
And look at where I am.

1186
01:13:17,160 --> 01:13:20,080
I have played
a far more exciting game

1187
01:13:20,080 --> 01:13:22,520
than the two finalists
sitting next to me.

1188
01:13:23,520 --> 01:13:27,040
I didn't have time
to build shelters, make fires.

1189
01:13:27,040 --> 01:13:29,320
I was at Tribal Council
every second night

1190
01:13:29,320 --> 01:13:33,360
using that strategy that I had
learnt to succeed in this game

1191
01:13:33,360 --> 01:13:35,280
and get a day in deeper.

1192
01:13:36,480 --> 01:13:38,480
I'm the last-standing Villain.

1193
01:13:38,480 --> 01:13:43,240
I'm the last-standing
first-time female player.

1194
01:13:43,240 --> 01:13:46,440
I took down
the game's biggest villain,

1195
01:13:49,360 --> 01:13:52,640
And I perfectly balanced
being a hero,

1196
01:13:52,640 --> 01:13:55,600
wearing a purple,
glittery Villains cape

1197
01:13:55,600 --> 01:13:59,600
and that is why I am in pole
position to be Sole Survivor.

1198
01:14:02,920 --> 01:14:05,200
(REFLECTIVE MUSIC)

1199
01:14:13,480 --> 01:14:18,120
Alright, jury, you should have all
the information you need now

1200
01:14:18,120 --> 01:14:22,480
to decide who you think
deserves the title of Sole Survivor

1201
01:14:22,480 --> 01:14:25,240
and the half-million dollars
that goes with it.

1202
01:14:26,280 --> 01:14:30,200
Remember, tonight,
you are voting for a winner.

1203
01:14:31,520 --> 01:14:33,120
For the last time,

1204
01:14:33,120 --> 01:14:35,400
it is time to vote.

1205
01:14:35,400 --> 01:14:37,560
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

1206
01:14:39,520 --> 01:14:41,320
(UNEASY MUSIC)

1207
01:14:48,000 --> 01:14:50,960
(TENSE MUSIC)

1208
01:14:57,640 --> 01:15:01,040
(TRIBAL SINGING)

1209
01:15:02,040 --> 01:15:03,640
JONATHAN: For the last time,

1210
01:15:03,640 --> 01:15:06,400
it is...time to vote.

1211
01:15:07,560 --> 01:15:09,640
Hayley, you're up.

1212
01:15:09,640 --> 01:15:12,360
(DRAMATIC MUSIC)

1213
01:15:39,600 --> 01:15:41,360
(SIGHS)

1214
01:16:09,200 --> 01:16:10,400
George, you're up.

1215
01:16:24,600 --> 01:16:27,160
I taught you to be ruthless.

1216
01:16:28,920 --> 01:16:31,200
And I taught you
how to be a villain.

1217
01:16:33,400 --> 01:16:36,480
And I couldn't be more proud
to vote for you.

1218
01:16:39,280 --> 01:16:42,560
The worthy winner
of Heroes v Villains.

1219
01:16:42,560 --> 01:16:45,360
(TENSE MUSIC)

1220
01:16:48,640 --> 01:16:50,880
I'll go count the votes.

1221
01:17:13,640 --> 01:17:15,080
I just wanna say,

1222
01:17:15,080 --> 01:17:17,720
this has really been
an incredible season.

1223
01:17:17,720 --> 01:17:19,200
So much fun.

1224
01:17:19,200 --> 01:17:20,680
Everyone, well done.

1225
01:17:20,680 --> 01:17:21,680
Seriously.

1226
01:17:21,680 --> 01:17:23,160
NINA: Thank you.
GEORGE: Thank you!

1227
01:17:23,160 --> 01:17:24,520
Thank you.

1228
01:17:25,520 --> 01:17:29,960
Alright, the only thing left
to do now is read the votes.

1229
01:17:29,960 --> 01:17:32,400
But a moment like this
really should be shared

1230
01:17:32,400 --> 01:17:34,240
with some of the people
you love the most.

1231
01:17:34,240 --> 01:17:37,240
Oh, my God!
So, come on in!

1232
01:17:38,400 --> 01:17:40,480
(HEARTWARMING MUSIC)

1233
01:17:40,480 --> 01:17:41,680
PAM: Hello!

1234
01:17:41,680 --> 01:17:43,400
Hi.

1235
01:17:43,400 --> 01:17:46,480
(LIZ SOBS)
You're a survivor.

1236
01:17:55,280 --> 01:17:57,120
(LIZ GIGGLES)

1237
01:17:57,120 --> 01:17:59,160
Alright, let's get to it.

1238
01:18:00,240 --> 01:18:02,760
Remember, these votes
are for a winner.

1239
01:18:05,080 --> 01:18:06,680
I'm gonna read the votes.

1240
01:18:11,360 --> 01:18:12,840
(TENSE MUSIC)

1241
01:18:13,840 --> 01:18:16,000
First vote.

1242
01:18:16,960 --> 01:18:17,960
Liz.

1243
01:18:26,040 --> 01:18:27,040
Liz.

1244
01:18:28,080 --> 01:18:29,560
That's two votes Liz.

1245
01:18:33,680 --> 01:18:35,960
Liz.

1246
01:18:37,080 --> 01:18:38,640
That's three votes Liz.

1247
01:18:43,200 --> 01:18:46,120
Winner of Australian Survivor
Heroes v Villains...

1248
01:18:47,200 --> 01:18:48,440
..Liz!

1249
01:18:49,520 --> 01:18:51,600
(ALL CHEER)

1250
01:18:51,600 --> 01:18:54,360
(TRIUMPHANT MUSIC)

1251
01:18:54,360 --> 01:18:56,720
(ALL CONTINUE CHEERING)

1252
01:18:58,000 --> 01:18:59,920
Let's go, let's go, let's go!

1253
01:18:59,920 --> 01:19:01,400
DANIEL: Well done.

1254
01:19:01,400 --> 01:19:03,920
(CHEERING CONTINUES)

1255
01:19:03,920 --> 01:19:05,360
DANIEL: Well done.

1256
01:19:05,360 --> 01:19:07,720
GEORGE: Congrats!
I'm so proud of you.

1257
01:19:10,360 --> 01:19:12,360
(ALL SPEAK EXCITEDLY)
Seriously.

1258
01:19:12,360 --> 01:19:15,320
Liz, congratulations.
Thank you, Jonathan!

1259
01:19:15,320 --> 01:19:17,800
You are Australia's Sole Survivor...

1260
01:19:17,800 --> 01:19:19,840
(ALL CHEER)
..Heroes v Villains.

1261
01:19:19,840 --> 01:19:21,880
Well played.

1262
01:19:21,880 --> 01:19:23,920
(ALL CHEER)

1263
01:19:23,920 --> 01:19:25,360
(LAUGHTER)

1264
01:19:27,080 --> 01:19:28,480
Whoo!
(JONATHAN LAUGHS)

1265
01:19:30,200 --> 01:19:31,880
(CHEERING CONTINUES)

1266
01:19:31,880 --> 01:19:33,760
(TRIUMPHANT MUSIC)

1267
01:19:35,480 --> 01:19:37,600
I actually cannot believe it.

1268
01:19:38,600 --> 01:19:41,400
I can't believe I'm here.

1269
01:19:41,400 --> 01:19:43,200
And I can't believe I won.

1270
01:19:44,200 --> 01:19:46,920
Liz, I taught you to be ruthless

1271
01:19:46,920 --> 01:19:50,480
and I taught you how to be a villain
and look what you did to me.

1272
01:19:50,480 --> 01:19:52,880
And you're the only person
to ever vote me out.

1273
01:19:52,880 --> 01:19:55,560
I couldn't be more proud
to vote for you,

1274
01:19:55,560 --> 01:19:58,280
the worthy winner
of Heroes v Villains.

1275
01:19:58,280 --> 01:19:59,280
(KISSES)

1276
01:19:59,280 --> 01:20:04,040
My strategy to get to the end
was to play hard, to take risks

1277
01:20:04,040 --> 01:20:10,160
and to push myself physically,
socially and mentally.

1278
01:20:10,160 --> 01:20:12,760
Honestly, playing in Survivor

1279
01:20:12,760 --> 01:20:15,280
is 10 times harder
than going to the Olympics.

1280
01:20:15,280 --> 01:20:17,640
You have played a remarkable game.

1281
01:20:17,640 --> 01:20:19,680
Not only do you show attributes

1282
01:20:19,680 --> 01:20:24,320
of a villain, of a hero
and of a vigilante,

1283
01:20:24,320 --> 01:20:26,840
but also of a great Survivor player.

1284
01:20:26,840 --> 01:20:29,200
You were ruthless
when you needed to be.

1285
01:20:29,200 --> 01:20:32,400
You absolutely hit this game
out of the park.

1286
01:20:32,400 --> 01:20:33,600
Well done.

1287
01:20:33,600 --> 01:20:35,360
I think I'll be remembered

1288
01:20:35,360 --> 01:20:39,200
as someone that played
an authentic game,

1289
01:20:39,200 --> 01:20:41,960
someone that stayed true
to themselves

1290
01:20:41,960 --> 01:20:45,360
and someone that was
a fierce player.

1291
01:20:46,360 --> 01:20:49,480
This moment is gonna change
my life forever.

1292
01:20:49,480 --> 01:20:51,200
Congratulations.

1293
01:20:51,200 --> 01:20:56,080
In a season where new players,
villains and women

1294
01:20:56,080 --> 01:20:58,480
were endangered species,

1295
01:20:58,480 --> 01:21:00,800
maybe the combination of all three

1296
01:21:00,800 --> 01:21:03,480
is exactly what we needed
to rise to the top.

1297
01:21:03,480 --> 01:21:04,720
Well done.

1298
01:21:20,080 --> 01:21:22,080
Captions by Red Bee Media



## S11E24

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,162
WWW.MY-SUBS.CO

1
00:00:05,260 --> 00:00:09,620
JONATHAN LAPAGLIA: 12 Titans
at the top of their game...

2
00:00:09,620 --> 00:00:12,300
VIOLA: Titans are a force
to be reckoned with.

3
00:00:12,300 --> 00:00:14,540
Go, go, go, go, go, go, go, go!
Yeah!

4
00:00:14,540 --> 00:00:16,100
A tribe of need leaders.

5
00:00:16,100 --> 00:00:18,380
Come on, boys!
(CHEERING)

6
00:00:18,380 --> 00:00:20,540
..took on 12 Rebels...

7
00:00:20,540 --> 00:00:21,980
(SHOUTING)

8
00:00:21,980 --> 00:00:25,140
..determined to play
by their own rules...

9
00:00:25,140 --> 00:00:27,220
(CHEERING)

10
00:00:27,220 --> 00:00:29,340
It was perfect Rebel behaviour.

11
00:00:29,340 --> 00:00:30,580
(CHEERING)

12
00:00:30,580 --> 00:00:32,580
I was way too freaking rebellious!

13
00:00:32,580 --> 00:00:34,220
Om.

14
00:00:34,220 --> 00:00:36,740
..each ready to outwit...

15
00:00:36,740 --> 00:00:39,500
A bloody idol, baby! (LAUGHS)

16
00:00:39,500 --> 00:00:44,100
My idol has saved me through more
than a dozen Tribal Councils.

17
00:00:44,100 --> 00:00:46,780
Did Ray just fake-find the idol?

18
00:00:46,780 --> 00:00:48,740
They don't vote with us,
then Caroline goes home.

19
00:00:48,740 --> 00:00:50,780
Yeah.
Because I will vote with them.

20
00:00:50,780 --> 00:00:52,820
I'm delivering my first blindside.

21
00:00:52,820 --> 00:00:55,300
And guess what? It's a baby girl.

22
00:00:55,300 --> 00:00:57,460
..outplay...

23
00:01:02,140 --> 00:01:03,660
I'm gonna demolish everyone.

24
00:01:03,660 --> 00:01:06,780
My vote tonight is the weakest
link in our tribe.

25
00:01:06,780 --> 00:01:10,100
They say that Val fights
wolves in Russia,

26
00:01:10,100 --> 00:01:13,980
but wolves are just puppy dogs
compared to me.

27
00:01:13,980 --> 00:01:15,580
..and outlast.

28
00:01:15,580 --> 00:01:19,260
We have a showdown
between Mark and Feras.

29
00:01:19,260 --> 00:01:20,460
Yes! Whoo-hoo!

30
00:01:20,460 --> 00:01:23,420
This could be
a half-million-dollar shot.

31
00:01:24,500 --> 00:01:25,980
Yeah!

32
00:01:25,980 --> 00:01:29,300
Mark takes individual immunity again!

33
00:01:29,300 --> 00:01:31,340
From fierce rivalries...

34
00:01:31,340 --> 00:01:33,060
(LAUGHS)
Now, you tried to get me again.

35
00:01:33,060 --> 00:01:34,060
I did, I did.

36
00:01:34,060 --> 00:01:36,620
In the mafia, if somebody goes
for the boss,

37
00:01:36,620 --> 00:01:38,260
like, you've got to take them out.

38
00:01:38,260 --> 00:01:42,380
My alliance and Feras's alliance
are gunning for each other.

39
00:01:42,380 --> 00:01:45,100
Kirby, right now,
is bloody untouchable.

40
00:01:45,100 --> 00:01:47,860
I think that we have too many people
in this tribe that are scared

41
00:01:47,860 --> 00:01:49,580
to write her name down.

42
00:01:49,580 --> 00:01:51,140
Just leave my name out of it.

43
00:01:52,380 --> 00:01:55,220
..they formed loyal alliances.

44
00:01:55,220 --> 00:01:58,140
I want to try to find a way
to come back together.

45
00:01:58,140 --> 00:01:59,180
Mm-hm.

46
00:01:59,180 --> 00:02:01,740
I, as a former diplomat,
bring people together.

47
00:02:01,740 --> 00:02:03,540
New beginnings.
New beginnings, new beginnings.

48
00:02:03,540 --> 00:02:04,540
New beginnings.

49
00:02:04,540 --> 00:02:06,260
Kirby feels like an older sister.

50
00:02:06,260 --> 00:02:07,500
We think alike.

51
00:02:07,500 --> 00:02:09,740
Who would you want to sit
next to at the end?

52
00:02:09,740 --> 00:02:11,060
You, Ri, or Kitty?

53
00:02:12,180 --> 00:02:15,740
Serious?
I want to beat the best of the best.

54
00:02:15,740 --> 00:02:18,180
And after 45 days...

55
00:02:18,180 --> 00:02:20,780
You're all about to really hate me.
Oh, no way!

56
00:02:20,780 --> 00:02:23,700
Valeria.
OTHERS: Oh!

57
00:02:23,700 --> 00:02:24,980
..and countless blindsides...

58
00:02:24,980 --> 00:02:26,540
I'm going to play it for Mark.

59
00:02:26,540 --> 00:02:27,660
Thank you.

60
00:02:27,660 --> 00:02:29,220
Tonight I'm backing myself.

61
00:02:29,220 --> 00:02:30,420
I'd like to play this for me.

62
00:02:32,060 --> 00:02:34,140
Kirby, the tribe has spoken.

63
00:02:34,140 --> 00:02:35,580
They have.

64
00:02:35,580 --> 00:02:37,820
..the final three...

65
00:02:37,820 --> 00:02:39,060
Feras could have saved Kirby.

66
00:02:39,060 --> 00:02:41,260
He had an idol.
He didn't play it for her.

67
00:02:41,260 --> 00:02:42,540
It has been a regret of mine.

68
00:02:42,540 --> 00:02:46,180
If I'd kept Kirby, she would be
wearing that necklace today, 100%.

69
00:02:46,180 --> 00:02:49,500
..were decided by fire.

70
00:02:49,500 --> 00:02:52,380
Caroline wins her position

71
00:02:52,380 --> 00:02:54,020
in the final three.
Well done.

72
00:02:54,020 --> 00:02:55,500
Argh!

73
00:03:00,380 --> 00:03:02,540
Raymond, the tribe has spoken.

74
00:03:03,820 --> 00:03:05,460
Three are left.

75
00:03:05,460 --> 00:03:08,900
Who will become Sole Survivor?

76
00:03:39,900 --> 00:03:41,460
FERAS: I feel extremely numb.

77
00:03:46,220 --> 00:03:47,780
(CAROLINE CHUCKLES)

78
00:03:54,460 --> 00:03:55,980
I've lost everything.

79
00:04:00,700 --> 00:04:03,020
I chose to back myself.

80
00:04:04,380 --> 00:04:06,660
And when it comes to challenges...

81
00:04:07,860 --> 00:04:09,780
..I've fallen extremely short.

82
00:04:11,940 --> 00:04:15,340
I have not won a single
individual immunity.

83
00:04:17,780 --> 00:04:22,220
And I know Mark's extremely tough
when it comes to his mental state.

84
00:04:24,460 --> 00:04:27,260
But I'm gonna dig deep.

85
00:04:29,820 --> 00:04:32,420
I'm going to be thinking of my wife

86
00:04:32,420 --> 00:04:37,140
and everyone back home
in Western Sydney,

87
00:04:37,140 --> 00:04:40,180
and I want to make sure
I make them all proud.

88
00:04:43,580 --> 00:04:45,580
My back's against the wall now.

89
00:04:46,700 --> 00:04:47,780
I've got no other choice.

90
00:04:49,300 --> 00:04:52,500
It's either win today's
challenge or go home.

91
00:04:54,220 --> 00:04:55,300
I'm in trouble.

92
00:05:05,140 --> 00:05:07,300
MARK: Dreams can come true.

93
00:05:07,300 --> 00:05:11,340
It is day 46 on Survivor,

94
00:05:11,340 --> 00:05:13,460
and I am the top three.

95
00:05:18,900 --> 00:05:23,380
Last night at Tribal Council,
we sent Ray packing to the jury

96
00:05:23,380 --> 00:05:25,860
in a fire-making challenge,

97
00:05:25,860 --> 00:05:28,100
and I landed some big right hooks

98
00:05:28,100 --> 00:05:29,580
on Feras's chin.

99
00:05:31,580 --> 00:05:33,420
It was a great feeling for me.

100
00:05:34,580 --> 00:05:36,580
I've totally rattled him.

101
00:05:38,780 --> 00:05:41,980
I came to this game
as a former diplomat.

102
00:05:41,980 --> 00:05:43,820
I used all of my skills -

103
00:05:43,820 --> 00:05:46,100
I analysed, I strategised,

104
00:05:46,100 --> 00:05:48,980
and, at times, I put aside
my personal feelings

105
00:05:48,980 --> 00:05:51,980
to get enemies to work together.

106
00:05:51,980 --> 00:05:53,580
That is diplomacy 101.

107
00:05:59,260 --> 00:06:03,260
But the fact that I haven't
been afraid to instigate conflict

108
00:06:03,260 --> 00:06:05,940
proves that I am a ruthless player,

109
00:06:05,940 --> 00:06:07,940
and I will destroy anyone

110
00:06:07,940 --> 00:06:09,060
to win this game.

111
00:06:10,580 --> 00:06:15,900
It's been 46 days of blood, sweat
and tears, out here on this island.

112
00:06:15,900 --> 00:06:18,460
I've won two immunity challenges
in a row,

113
00:06:18,460 --> 00:06:21,940
and now I am gonna win this final
immunity challenge.

114
00:06:23,060 --> 00:06:25,220
The time for diplomacy is over.

115
00:06:25,220 --> 00:06:28,140
All that remains is me going to war.

116
00:06:28,140 --> 00:06:31,420
(DRAMATIC MUSIC PLAYS)

117
00:06:38,580 --> 00:06:40,180
CAROLINE: Being an older woman,

118
00:06:40,180 --> 00:06:42,780
I know that my tribe might
have looked at me

119
00:06:42,780 --> 00:06:43,940
as a weak link.

120
00:06:44,940 --> 00:06:46,860
They all underestimated me.

121
00:06:51,940 --> 00:06:54,540
But I've been playing the long game.

122
00:06:55,820 --> 00:06:58,220
When I have a goal in mind,

123
00:06:58,220 --> 00:07:00,460
I will do everything to get there,

124
00:07:00,460 --> 00:07:04,100
and I don't think
that they expect that in me.

125
00:07:05,300 --> 00:07:07,620
I took out massive threats.

126
00:07:08,580 --> 00:07:11,260
I split up power couples.

127
00:07:11,260 --> 00:07:14,220
I wasn't going to let anything
get in the way

128
00:07:14,220 --> 00:07:17,540
of me getting to here, right now.

129
00:07:23,340 --> 00:07:26,340
We've got two Titans and one Rebel.

130
00:07:26,340 --> 00:07:30,580
And today, it's all going to hinge
on this final immunity challenge.

131
00:07:31,980 --> 00:07:37,020
I know that if I don't win it,
Mark will take me to the final two.

132
00:07:38,380 --> 00:07:40,580
The power lies with Mark and I...

133
00:07:41,940 --> 00:07:43,860
..so Feras better watch out.

134
00:08:11,820 --> 00:08:12,820
Oh, dear Lord.

135
00:08:15,140 --> 00:08:18,020
(CREAKING)

136
00:08:18,020 --> 00:08:19,700
(EERIE MUSIC PLAYS)

137
00:08:23,900 --> 00:08:25,260
Come on in.

138
00:08:39,700 --> 00:08:41,780
(VOCALISING)

139
00:08:46,820 --> 00:08:48,340
Congratulations.

140
00:08:48,340 --> 00:08:51,220
You've made it to day 46.

141
00:08:51,220 --> 00:08:56,260
And to get this far, you've survived
a clash of Titans and Rebels,

142
00:08:56,260 --> 00:08:59,940
in a season that has produced
some of the most intense

143
00:08:59,940 --> 00:09:02,620
and unpredictable gameplay
we've ever seen,

144
00:09:02,620 --> 00:09:04,260
so well done.

145
00:09:04,260 --> 00:09:06,620
Thank you, JLP.
Thank you. Thank you.

146
00:09:06,620 --> 00:09:09,900
Now, are you ready to get
to your final immunity challenge?

147
00:09:09,900 --> 00:09:11,580
Yes.
Alright.

148
00:09:13,540 --> 00:09:15,700
Here, JLP.
Thank you, Mark.

149
00:09:18,580 --> 00:09:22,420
For the last time, immunity
is back up for grabs.

150
00:09:22,420 --> 00:09:23,740
For today's challenge...

151
00:09:27,060 --> 00:09:31,220
..you're gonna stand on narrow pegs
fixed to a giant wheel.

152
00:09:33,100 --> 00:09:35,620
At regular intervals,
the wheel will turn...

153
00:09:35,620 --> 00:09:37,260
(WHEEL CREAKS)

154
00:09:40,420 --> 00:09:43,060
..forcing you onto narrower pegs.

155
00:09:48,380 --> 00:09:50,820
If at any point
you come off the wheel,

156
00:09:50,820 --> 00:09:52,460
you're out of the challenge.

157
00:09:52,460 --> 00:09:56,980
Last person left standing
wins immunity and is guaranteed

158
00:09:56,980 --> 00:09:59,420
a spot at that final Tribal Council,

159
00:09:59,420 --> 00:10:03,500
where you will have a chance to pitch
to the jury why you deserve

160
00:10:03,500 --> 00:10:04,820
the title of Sole Survivor

161
00:10:04,820 --> 00:10:06,660
and the half a million dollars
that goes with it.

162
00:10:06,660 --> 00:10:08,940
Yeah.

163
00:10:08,940 --> 00:10:12,100
In addition, you'll also get
to decide who will be sitting

164
00:10:12,100 --> 00:10:14,380
next to you at that Tribal Council.

165
00:10:16,980 --> 00:10:20,820
Now, there's a lot on the line,
and this is a tough challenge.

166
00:10:20,820 --> 00:10:24,460
So, we figured that you might need
a little extra motivation

167
00:10:24,460 --> 00:10:26,860
from some loved ones.
Oh.

168
00:10:26,860 --> 00:10:29,780
Mark, who are you hoping
to see today?

169
00:10:29,780 --> 00:10:31,140
My wife, Sas.

170
00:10:39,020 --> 00:10:40,460
(CRIES, LAUGHS)

171
00:10:47,500 --> 00:10:48,780
Oh, my gosh!

172
00:10:58,460 --> 00:11:00,300
I'm doing good.

173
00:11:00,300 --> 00:11:02,540
Give me a kiss. Sorry, I probably
stink. Come on over.

174
00:11:02,540 --> 00:11:03,860
No, you're fine.

175
00:11:03,860 --> 00:11:05,780
Come meet my mates.
Oh, my gosh, yes.

176
00:11:05,780 --> 00:11:07,140
This is JLP.
Hi.

177
00:11:07,140 --> 00:11:08,540
Hi.

178
00:11:08,540 --> 00:11:10,620
And this is Feras and Caroline.
Hi!

179
00:11:10,620 --> 00:11:13,380
Hey, Sas.
Nice to meet you.

180
00:11:13,380 --> 00:11:16,500
He and I have had our ups and downs,
but we love each other, right now.

181
00:11:16,500 --> 00:11:18,340
(LAUGHTER)
Sorry!

182
00:11:18,340 --> 00:11:23,820
So, Mark, how does it feel seeing
Saskia for the first time in 46 days?

183
00:11:23,820 --> 00:11:26,580
It's just so special to have her
here right now.

184
00:11:26,580 --> 00:11:29,020
There's no one else I want here
more than Sas.

185
00:11:29,020 --> 00:11:32,820
I'm going to have to have the fight
of my life on that thing.

186
00:11:32,820 --> 00:11:34,980
And I know that Sas is going
to give me the strength to win.

187
00:11:34,980 --> 00:11:36,340
That's what I need right now.

188
00:11:37,820 --> 00:11:40,460
Just so glad you're here.
Can't stop looking at you.

189
00:11:40,460 --> 00:11:42,140
I know, look at me.
(ALL LAUGH)

190
00:11:45,860 --> 00:11:47,620
Alright, Caroline, are you ready
for some love?

191
00:11:48,860 --> 00:11:51,380
Oh, Jonathan. Yep.

192
00:11:51,380 --> 00:11:52,780
Come on in.

193
00:12:01,700 --> 00:12:03,340
(BOTH CRY, LAUGH)

194
00:12:07,500 --> 00:12:09,500
It's so good to see you.

195
00:12:17,860 --> 00:12:18,940
Yeah.

196
00:12:18,940 --> 00:12:21,260
Yeah, last night was crazy.
Oh, yeah.

197
00:12:24,820 --> 00:12:26,340
This is my husband, Murray.

198
00:12:26,340 --> 00:12:28,780
Hi, really nice to meet you.
Yes, hello.

199
00:12:28,780 --> 00:12:30,420
Oh.
Wow.

200
00:12:32,500 --> 00:12:34,740
So, Murray, when Caroline
came to you and said,

201
00:12:34,740 --> 00:12:37,100
"You know, I'm just going to go
and play Survivor,"

202
00:12:37,100 --> 00:12:38,300
what did you think?

203
00:12:38,300 --> 00:12:39,380
Um...

204
00:12:40,660 --> 00:12:43,660
..I think I started off with,
like, "What, seriously?"

205
00:12:43,660 --> 00:12:47,380
And this is a person who loves
a silk pillow,

206
00:12:47,380 --> 00:12:52,460
an eye mask, earplugs
and a really puffy, comfortable bed.

207
00:12:53,860 --> 00:12:55,780
But she just wanted to prove
to herself, I think,

208
00:12:55,780 --> 00:12:57,340
that she could get outside
of her comfort zone

209
00:12:57,340 --> 00:12:58,500
and actually do this.

210
00:12:58,500 --> 00:13:00,340
So, I mean, I'm not surprised
that she's here,

211
00:13:00,340 --> 00:13:02,700
and I'm not surprised
that she's done really well.

212
00:13:02,700 --> 00:13:05,220
He knows how much I wanted
to be here.

213
00:13:05,220 --> 00:13:09,980
So to have him here and know
that he's very proud of me,

214
00:13:09,980 --> 00:13:12,100
yeah, it's amazing! (LAUGHS)

215
00:13:12,100 --> 00:13:13,540
Certainly is.

216
00:13:18,700 --> 00:13:21,460
Alright, Feras, I know
that you've been missing home.

217
00:13:21,460 --> 00:13:22,980
Who are you hoping to see?

218
00:13:22,980 --> 00:13:25,700
Um... (CRIES) ..my wife.

219
00:13:25,700 --> 00:13:27,580
I'm dying to see her.

220
00:13:27,580 --> 00:13:29,140
Alright, come on in.

221
00:13:36,860 --> 00:13:38,180
Oh. (LAUGHS)

222
00:13:48,500 --> 00:13:50,580
(BOTH CRY)

223
00:14:04,940 --> 00:14:06,580
Stop.

224
00:14:06,580 --> 00:14:09,020
Look how skinny I am.
(LAUGHTER)

225
00:14:09,020 --> 00:14:10,420
Oh, my God.

226
00:14:10,420 --> 00:14:12,020
I'm literally shaking.

227
00:14:12,020 --> 00:14:13,740
Guys...
Oh, my God, hi.

228
00:14:13,740 --> 00:14:15,660
..this is my lovely wife, Iman.

229
00:14:17,140 --> 00:14:19,300
Oh, my God, I missed you so much.
Oh, wow.

230
00:14:19,300 --> 00:14:22,100
Feras, how much have you missed
your wife?

231
00:14:22,100 --> 00:14:24,460
She's all I've ever thought
about this whole time.

232
